title: Experiment with same-frame deoptimization without an ABI cut (Design 74F)
description:
# 74F — Same-frame deoptimization without an ABI cut

Status: experiment authorized 2026-09-10; protocol below recorded before running.
The user selected the second path after the 74E reversal: preserve the current
runtime ABI, image format, and Frame representation while proving recovery.

## Problem and scope

74A–74D prove fallback before an individual operation. They do not demonstrate
switching an active optimized computation back to its original implementation.
74E's new generated-code exports are not needed for a runtime-owned experiment.

This experiment uses the real Runtime driver, registered native StepMethods,
and descriptor-v2 Frames. It runs in the Rust test harness: a test-only private
tier record selects between two statically linked native entries. There is no
new export, compiler emission, artifact tier, saved metadata, or installed mode.
Hand-authored entries deliberately isolate recovery from compiler construction.
This is a recovery experiment, not a speed or general-optimizer qualification.

## Mechanism and equivalence

One runtime-local record retains the exact baseline descriptor by `Arc`, one
static optimized entry, an epoch, and a bounded list of eligible PCs. Selection
occurs after allocation of the existing resume token and before native entry.
It checks the exact descriptor allocation, PC, current dictionary epoch, and
74A's canonical Machine/lookup guard. An exhausted epoch never authorizes the
optimized entry. A failed dependency check permanently disables this trial;
the driver invokes the descriptor's original StepMethod with the same token.
No state borrow crosses entry or an ordinary send.

Both entries use the same descriptor, PC meanings, live-slot bitmap and ordinary
action publication. The optimized entry removes a second identical slot read
within an allocation-free, callback-free region whose Machine lookup is guarded.
The baseline reuses the already-boxed index for both reads. The optimized entry
does not carry assumptions across the later effect callback or any allocation.
Subsequent writes and action publication use ordinary sends.

PC 0 computes a value, stores it and an alias in canonical rooted slots, then
performs one effect callback. That callback may change lookup or replace the
currently active method. Both versions publish the same Continue edge to PC 1.
At PC 1 the driver can select the original baseline entry without copying or
reconstructing a Frame. The identity mapping is the recovery map: the next PC,
live Oops, aliases, return destination and active implementation stay in place.
Replacing a method binding must affect the next invocation, not replace the
already-active baseline body. Existing registration pins protect that body.

The tier owns no Oop roots or dynamically allocated executable code. Its only
candidate is a static test function. Retaining an `Arc<FrameDescriptor>` would
not by itself protect a dynamically unloadable code generation; admission and
leases for such candidates are explicitly outside this experiment.

## Frozen acceptance checks

- Run baseline and candidate independently; compare answers and effect traces.
- Prove optimized entry actually executes and removes the redundant read.
- Force invalidation after the effect; observe optimized PC 0 then baseline
  PC 1 on the same generational Frame handle and descriptor.
- Check no repeated effect or argument evaluation; preserve carried values and
  alias identity across recovery.
- Cover canonical execution, pre-entry invalidation, mutation then restoration,
  custom lookup, Machine override, and active method replacement. A later send
  must see the replacement while the active call finishes its original body.
- Force precise collection while values are retained only through the Frame;
  check a retained FrameView and its invalidation after return.
- Exercise nested registered entry and repeated trials; all Frames and pins
  must be released. Candidate selection must not attach to a different
  descriptor merely because its numeric identity matches.
- Leave runtime ABI inputs, IdApi, image/descriptor codecs and fixtures byte
  unchanged. Ordinary builds must contain no experiment code or exports.

## Running and results

Implementation, reproduction command, and measured results will be recorded
here after the experiment. Success establishes recovery at existing committed
StepMethod boundaries with canonical Frame storage. Mid-activation exits,
register recovery, inlined frames, eliminated objects, arbitrary FFI unwinding,
and image persistence of an optimized tier remain outside the result.
notes: Executed Design 74F. Ten real-driver baseline/candidate cases and 256 repeated trials pass identically in debug and release. Same Frame, original implementation, carried values, aliases, effect order, custom lookup, precise GC, nested entry and pin cleanup checked. No ABI/image/descriptor changes; test-only static native entries. Receipt: docs/measurements/74f-same-frame-deopt.json. Full mise run verify passed. No application performance claim or production activation.

title: Experiment with compiler-generated same-frame recovery (Design 74G)
description:
# 74G — Compiler-generated same-frame recovery

Status: experiment authorized 2026-09-10 after committing 74F as `43935092`.
This protocol is recorded before implementation and execution.

## Problem and proposed solution

74F switched between hand-written, statically linked entries. This experiment
starts with one canonical CodeProgram, uses the production portable lowering,
slot coloring, descriptor-v2 construction and C emitter, compiles native code,
and proves recovery and executable lifetime through the real Runtime driver.

The first optimization is **program-counter specialization**. A candidate entry
contains exactly one existing basic block and retains the ordinary argument-count
check. Runtime selection already knows the committed PC, so that entry omits the
resume-token decode and switch. Its operations, sends, allocation order, action
publication and shared descriptor remain unchanged. No assumption is carried
across a callback inside the body. The driver allocates the normal resume token,
checks the exact descriptor, PC and frozen dependency epoch, and pins the selected
native unit before entering it. Invalidation selects the original whole-method
entry, with the same Frame and PC.

This small optimization deliberately isolates the new compiler/runtime contract.
It is not the 74D boxed-index optimization. New slot helpers, changed IdApi fields,
image versions, descriptor formats and persisted optimization state are excluded.
The compiler entry point is development-feature-only; Runtime selection and the
native loader adapter are test-only. Ordinary emitted C must remain byte-identical.

## Input and admission

The fixture is a canonical CodeProgram built using the existing pure compiler
AST-to-portable encoder. Its Birnam meaning is:

```birnam
[:input |
  let carried := [input probeDouble]
  let alias := carried
  [Probe probeEffect: carried alias: alias]
  [Probe probeFinish: carried alias: alias]]
```

The source parser is not under test; the canonical program bytes are the actual
input. Both versions lower those same bytes and use one physical layout. Their
canonical descriptor bytes must agree exactly. The admission record retains
the program digest, descriptor bytes, exact baseline descriptor allocation and
dense PC-to-candidate-entry mapping. A mismatched descriptor or absent/out-of-range
PC must not authorize a candidate. The program's actual colored slots and edge
copy/clear plans, rather than 74F's hand-authored uniform bitmap, govern recovery.

## Native lifetime

Baseline and candidate are separate temporary native libraries. A fixture-local
adapter supplies the existing generated-code shim signatures through function
pointers; it creates no runtime exports and changes no frozen API. The adapter
is not a production artifact-admission mechanism.

The baseline owner holds an existing registration-generation lease token. The
Runtime keeps that token while bindings, acquisitions, Frames or continuations
can still enter the generation. Withdrawing a binding is not permission to
unmap its code. The test owner may release the library only after retirement
and the token's other holders have gone. Candidate admission owns its library;
each selected entry also holds an independent native-code lease through return.
Withdrawing the candidate during a native shim call must not unmap the currently
executing entry. `dlclose` occurs after the last required owner releases it.

The experiment must verify actual unload calls and subsequent loader absence,
not only clear a Rust map or decrement a diagnostic count. Dynamic code is never
entered through an unowned pointer, and no Runtime borrow crosses a native call.

## Frozen checks

- Execute baseline and candidate from the same CodeProgram; require identical
  answers, once-only effect order and alias identity.
- Inspect emitted C to prove candidate entries omit PC decoding/switches while
  baseline emission remains byte-identical to the committed compiler.
- Force epoch invalidation after the effect, including method replacement and
  custom lookup; later sends see current behavior, while the active caller
  resumes its original body at the compiler-assigned continuation PC.
- Force precise GC and validate compiler-derived live slots through recovery.
- Reject mismatched descriptor bytes and invalid/missing candidate PC mappings.
- Withdraw candidate admission while its native entry is on stack; prove the
  current call remains mapped and the unit unloads only after return.
- Withdraw the baseline binding while its Frame is active; prove the generation
  remains mapped until the Frame and registration lease release it.
- Repeat load/execute/recover/retire cycles and check Frame, acquisition, native
  lease and loader cleanup. Run both debug and release Rust profiles.
- Preserve runtime ABI and image/descriptor authorities and golden fixtures;
  run ordinary compiler tests and the full repository verification gate.

## Measurement and limits

Record generated source sizes, native library sizes, compilation cost and warm
execution samples separately from correctness. Timings are diagnostic unless
the existing host gates permit a controlled comparison. Candidate activation
must be proven independently of elapsed time. No performance percentage is a
continuation threshold.

This remains a bounded experiment, not an installed optimizer. Source-parser
integration, production artifact admission, persistent optimized tiers, inlining,
eliminated objects and mid-native-activation recovery remain separate work.
notes: Completed Design 74G after committing 74F as 43935092. Twelve paired cases plus sixteen repeated native load/retire cycles pass in debug and release, with 84 confirmed unloads per profile including warm samples. Compiler-derived Frame slots, aliases, effect order, precise GC, descriptor/PC rejection, active binding replacement and executable retirement verified. Ordinary emitted C matches the committed golden; 61 compiler tests and 74F regression pass. Full mise run verify passes workspace, native-prefix, cold-archive and relocation gates. No ABI or image change; no production optimizer or speedup claim. Evidence: docs/design/74g-generated-same-frame-deoptimization.md and docs/measurements/74g-generated-frame-deopt.json. Committed as a10d1b55 before the authorized 74H experiment.

title: Implement and measure guarded Frame read reuse (Design 74H)
description:
# 74H — Guarded reuse of Frame reads

Status: authorized 2026-09-10 after committing 74G as `a10d1b55`.
This protocol precedes implementation and measurement.

## Problem and proposed solution

74G proves generated recovery and executable ownership. The next experiment
removes repeated ordinary Machine reads within one compiler basic block.
The comparator is 74G PC specialization with unchanged block bodies, so any
incremental benefit must pay for the new guard. Whole-method baseline emission
is a separate semantic reference.

The compiler identifies repeated reads of a physical slot with no intervening
compiler write to that slot. Eligible slots receive a native-local cache that
exists for one StepMethod invocation. The first read remains an ordinary send.
A later read may reuse its answer; all original index boxes, selector interning,
store operations, allocation order and action publication remain in place.
Ordinary emission and the existing descriptor bytes remain unchanged.

## Legality boundary

Dictionary epochs alone are insufficient. Index allocation can collect; a
native mark/finalization callback can change Frame contents without changing
method dictionaries. A test-only monotonically increasing GC epoch advances
before every mark traversal, including retirement reachability traversals.
It saturates, and its terminal value never admits reuse.

The read guard executes after the original read operands have been evaluated.
It checks canonical Machine identity, canonical read/write methods and lookup,
the dictionary epoch and the GC epoch. The first ordinary read is remembered
only if those conditions hold before its invocation. A mismatch permanently
disables that local cache for the remainder of this basic block; subsequent
reads use the ordinary send. Compiler stores invalidate a cache for their
destination slot. No cache survives an action return or crosses a language
send. The supported body consists of existing literal/global/binding operations
and call staging; nested block construction is excluded from this first slice.

Under the guard, the only calls between reads are native Integer allocation,
non-reentrant interning/import and canonical Machine slot operations. Collection
invalidates cached Oops before any reuse, so the cache introduces no extra root.
Every miss sends once with the already evaluated original operands. Driver
recovery uses 74G's exact descriptor and native-unit leases at the next boundary.

The helper is supplied through artifact-local test initialization, as a function
pointer. It is not a new floor export, IdApi field, runtime ABI version or image
format. Production admission is conditional follow-up work, not something this
test-local transport establishes.

## Frozen checks

- Compare whole-method baseline, PC-only control and read-reuse candidate.
- Check answers, argument identity/order, once-only effects and same-Frame PCs.
- Exercise no-repeat bodies and sparse/dense repeated-read bodies.
- Invalidate before entry, between repeated reads and on every measured call.
- Replace native Machine read/write methods and global lookup, including an
  override introduced after a read has already been cached.
- Force precise GC between reads; run a real root callback that changes the
  cached Frame slot without changing the dictionary epoch. Both old staged and
  newly read values must survive and appear in the expected argument order.
- Exercise collection with no mutation, epoch saturation, ordinary recovery,
  native retirement, and repeated runs with no remaining Frame/native leases.
- Retain 74F/74G regressions, ordinary compiler tests and full repository verify.

## Measurement and decision

Compile once before measuring, run release Rust with native `cc -O2`, and turn
off observation counters in timed samples. Prove activation separately. Use
fresh-process paired samples with alternating control/candidate order, warmup,
identical inputs, and the existing host preflight and interval-monitor gates.
Retain raw samples and compilation/native-size costs. Include 0, 2, 4 and 16
repeated arguments and ordinary, per-call invalidation and persistent fallback
conditions. Choose iteration counts before looking at comparative results.

Use seven pairs. A claimed improvement must exceed both variants' observed
within-variant sample range; report medians and ranges without a percentage
threshold. A regression beyond that same spread in any admitted shape or
invalidation/fallback condition prevents promotion of this implementation.
An inconclusive comparison does not count as a measured benefit.

If correctness and measurement justify it, continue with an opt-in normal
source/compiler/runtime integration using the current ABI. Otherwise retain
the experiment and its evidence, explain the limiting guard cost, and do not
silently widen assumptions or tune eligibility after seeing the results.
notes: Completed Design 74H after committing 74G as a10d1b55. The compiler reuses repeated physical-slot reads only within one PC under canonical Machine and dictionary/GC epoch guards, preserving index boxes, stores and misses. Debug/release agree on 36 observations and five groups of 64 additional calls; 82 native libraries unload per profile. A real GC root callback changes the source slot without changing the dictionary epoch; all variants correctly answer 119 instead of 224. Seven complete host-gated control/reuse pairs are inconclusive in all twelve timing rows under the frozen range criterion. Two earlier host-rejected partial attempts are retained separately. Normal source/compiler/runtime integration is deferred because no measured benefit cleared the criterion. The 61 ordinary compiler tests, 74F/74G regressions and full mise run verify pass. ABI/image authorities and fixtures are unchanged. Evidence: docs/design/74h-guarded-frame-read-reuse.md and docs/measurements/74h-frame-read-reuse.json. 74H committed as 5e242e70; followed by the external guard-boundary audit in Design 74I.
close_reason: Experiment complete: semantics, GC invalidation, native retirement and full verification pass; seven controlled timing pairs are inconclusive, so integration is not promoted.

title: Audit deoptimization guards through the frozen Id API (Design 74I)
description:
# 74I — Guard availability through the existing Id API

Status: experiment in progress after committing 74H as `5e242e70`.
The protocol below precedes implementation and execution.

## Problem and proposed solution

74F–74H prove recovery using private Runtime guards and test-only entry
selection. Before further optimization, determine whether the existing
interfaces can supply their guard authority to an ordinary native artifact.
The user requires work to stop at a necessary Id API, ABI or language-floor
change. A private function-pointer initializer avoids new exported names,
but does not by itself provide an ordinary floor implementation of that guard.

Run a C client through the frozen `IdApi` header against fresh, ordinary
debug/release floor builds. Use no development feature, private Rust access,
test driver or optimizer callback. This is a boundary experiment, not a
performance comparison or an attempted production optimizer.

## Frozen checks

- Replace a method while preserving receiver vtable identity and selector
  inventory; prove the subsequent ordinary send changes its answer.
- Change inheritance and add a shadowing method while observing the existing
  overwrite hook; prove those changes affect sends without notifying the hook.
- Replace that single hook; prove an earlier observer loses notifications.
- Install a forwarding global lookup with an observable effect. Compare one
  ordinary send with a proposed reflective guard followed by that same send.
  Preserve the answer and count the extra effect, including a lookup sent to
  the metatable itself.
- Collect with no change in live-object count or object vtable, while a real
  root callback changes a native object's payload. Check that a separate
  public root provider can observe the collection: absence of a public epoch
  does not imply absence of all external GC notification mechanisms.
- Check that ordinary floor builds do not export the experimental guarded
  slot helpers or the reverted 74E helpers.
- Run C at `-O0` and `-O2` against both floor profiles, in three fresh
  processes per combination. Require identical observations and retain
  source, compatibility, executable and floor hashes.

These checks can reject particular substitutes for the existing guards.
They cannot prove that every future compiler-only optimization is impossible.
If they expose a required floor mechanism, document that boundary and stop
before adding or promoting it.
notes: Completed external frozen-IdApi audit: eight cases agree in twelve fresh processes (debug/release floor, C O0/O2, three repetitions). Confirms method replacement without identity/inventory change, missed hook notifications, hook replacement, extra custom-lookup effects, GC mutation with equal live count, public GC notification and absent guard exports. No production floor source or ABI change. Production promotion stops before supplying private guard authority; a production optimizer remains incomplete. Evidence: docs/design/74i-public-api-guard-boundary.md and docs/measurements/74i-public-api-guard-boundary.json. User clarification 2026-09-11: runtime internals may change while API/ABI, full malleability and expressibility in Id semantics remain intact. The earlier blanket stop is superseded; 74J (birnam-internal-guarded-sends-xpn) implements guarded behavior inside ordinary sends. The 74I public-interface counterexamples remain valid.
close_reason: Boundary experiment complete: all external-client cases agree; production guard promotion stops at the user-declared floor/ABI boundary.

title: Promote guarded Machine sends inside the existing Id runtime (Design 74J)
description:
# 74J — Guarded Machine sends inside the existing runtime

Status: authorized by the user's 2026-09-11 clarification; implemented and
correctness-verified. The original longer E1 measurement remains unqualified
after two host-gate rejections. The combined 74J/74K/74L implementation later
meets the separate portable-fixture criterion in [74L](74l-guarded-default-lookup.md).
The protocol below preceded this change and its original measurements.

## Problem and scope

The user permits changes to runtime internals while preserving the public API,
ABI, full malleability and expressibility in Id-layer semantics. 74I's public
interface counterexamples therefore do not require stopping all runtime work.

The first production component is a guarded implementation of the existing
`oopAt:` and `oopAt:put:` sends inside `Runtime::send_abi`. Generated code and
native clients continue to issue exactly the same messages with the same
operands. The runtime may execute the canonical operation directly after a
non-effectful check, otherwise it follows the existing resolver and invocation
path. No new native helper, IdApi field, language selector, Frame layout,
descriptor, image hash or artifact registration contract is introduced.

This promotes guarded execution and immediate fallback for ordinary compiled
code. It does not by itself complete optimized native-tier admission from
74F/74G, or qualify 74H read caching. Runtime-owned native-tier admission is
subsequently implemented in [74K](74k-runtime-owned-native-tier.md); 74H read
caching remains deferred.

## Semantic obligations

- Preserve the send's argument-buffer validation and outer dispatch-read
  lease, including retirement processing when it ends.
- Optimize only the canonical Machine receiver and canonical read/write and
  lookup implementations. A private vtable, override, removal, inheritance
  change or custom lookup must retain ordinary dispatch and its effects.
- Do not cache Frame contents, operands, method results or a mutable Frame
  pointer. Index boxes and their allocation order remain unchanged.
- Retain canonical arity/type/index validation and every owner, capability,
  lifecycle, Frame-generation and slot-kind check.
- A method address registered as a resumable carrier must still pass through
  the ordinary resolver, even if its address equals a canonical floor method.
  Registration state is a separate dependency from dictionary mutation.
- A saturated dictionary epoch must not preserve an earlier cached verdict.
- The optimization is equivalent to the original Id send. It adds no
  primitive behavior that the original send cannot express.

## Validation and measurement protocol

Compare optimization enabled/disabled under a test-only control using the
same live Frame and native arguments. Prove activation independently of
answers. Cover valid and invalid access, mutation and restoration, native and
resumable replacement, custom lookup effects, private receiver vtables,
epoch saturation, GC mutation and native retirement. Retain existing ordinary
compiler, same-frame recovery and public-ABI tests. Full repository verification
must pass before promotion is reported as qualified.

Measure ordinary release builds of the baseline and candidate through the
same normal compiled source and existing IdApi. Use seven fresh-process pairs
with alternating order, the existing host preflight and interval gates, and
identical warmup/work. Include no-slot/ordinary-send controls, canonical slot
access and invalidated fallback. Keep instrumentation out of timed builds.
Claim a benefit only when the median improvement exceeds both variants'
observed sample ranges; a regression beyond that spread prevents default
promotion. Preserve all samples and unsuccessful host-gated attempts. Do not
change eligibility or comparison rules in response to the timing results.

## Implementation and correctness results

`Runtime::send_abi` now tries the canonical Machine access after validating
the argument buffer and entering its dispatch-read lease. The new
`runtime/guarded_dispatch.rs` module checks the selector and delegates to the
existing guarded boxed-index access. Every miss continues through the original
resolver. Wrong arity returns nil directly only after canonical eligibility
has been proved; an override still receives the original arguments.

The guard checks resumable registration independently of dictionary mutation.
A canonical function address registered as a resumable carrier is ineligible,
including an unpublished or retiring registration. The dictionary cache also
rechecks its conditions at a saturated mutation epoch. Neither check changes
the registration carrier or any execution-state layout visible to native code.

Three focused tests pass. The first compares ordinary and optimized dispatch
for nine live-Frame cases: canonical access, invalid operands, read and write
overrides, removed/inherited read, private receiver vtable, custom lookup,
epoch saturation, and GC mutation. It records guard hits separately from
answers and checks exact Frame identity and lookup/override effects. The other
tests cover registration without dictionary mutation, including invocation
through a real registered resumable replacement at a canonical function address.

The complete `birnam-id` suite passes (128 passed, seven ignored). The 74F,
74G and 74H correctness runners pass in debug and release; 74I's twelve ordinary
native-client processes also pass. These reruns preserve the original recovery,
precise-GC, registration and native-unload checks. Full `mise run verify`
passes, including workspace tests, normal native prefixes, two independent
fixture-free cold archives and relocated runtimes.
The [verification receipt](../measurements/74j-verification.json) records the
tested source hashes, command summaries and four retained regression receipts.

The E2 matrix has identical baseline/candidate output in all ten rows. This is
parity evidence: its two pre-existing abort cases still abort, and its
activate/rollback fixture does not report successful activation in either
prefix. It is not a new claim of successful activation from that fixture.

The older correctness runners now hash `execution.rs` as implementation input
instead of requiring its entire contents to remain frozen. Its only 74J change
is a private, non-mutating registration-presence query. The actual ABI, image,
descriptor and registration compatibility authorities remain byte-identical.

## Measurement execution

The runner is `scripts/internal-guarded-sends.py`. It compares a normal release
prefix built from `5e242e70` with a normal release prefix built from this change.
Both use `cargo build --workspace --locked --offline --release`. The generated
fixture imports the existing `birnam_send`; the floor export inventories agree
exactly. Canonical and native forwarding-lookup fallback modes run at 16,384
and 65,536 iterations, with an ordinary-send control at 100,000 iterations.

The [first attempt](../measurements/74j-internal-guarded-sends-rejected-1.json)
was rejected by the existing host interval gate during pair three: median idle
CPU was 11.44%, with 193 of 240 samples below 30%. All completed program checks
passed, but the attempt supplies no qualified performance comparison. The same
seven-pair protocol was repeated without changing thresholds or code. The
[second attempt](../measurements/74j-internal-guarded-sends-rejected-2.json) was
also rejected: pair two had median idle CPU of 18.39%, with 183 of 238 samples
below 30%. Timing qualification remains pending a quiet host; no performance
benefit or default-promotion acceptance is claimed from either attempt.
close_reason: Guarded ordinary Machine sends implemented and verified. Original long E1 attempts remain host-rejected; combined ordinary-prefix promotion is qualified separately by the retained 74L protocol.

title: Admit runtime-owned native PC entries through existing portable staging (Design 74K)
description:
# 74K — Runtime-owned native tier under the existing interfaces

Status: implemented and correctness-verified, 2026-09-11. Twelve baseline/
candidate registration cases pass, including same-Frame recovery, nested entry,
active replacement, GC and native-owner eviction. Full repository verification
and the ordinary-prefix materialization fixture pass. All fifteen comparisons
in the seven-group prefix measurement are inconclusive. PC specialization has
no independently qualified speedup. 74L investigates the remaining canonical
lookup cost; 74J's longer E1 timing remains unqualified after two host-gate rejections.

## Problem

74J can implement each ordinary Machine send more cheaply without asking a
native caller to know whether optimization is eligible. 74F–74H additionally
select specialized method bodies and reuse reads inside one PC. Their fixture
can call private Rust guards; an ordinary external compiler artifact cannot
obtain that authority through the existing interfaces without observable
lookup effects (74I).

The user's constraint permits internal runtime changes but requires the public
API, ABI, full malleability and expressibility in Id semantics to remain intact.
Adding helper exports, adding registration fields, repurposing reserved fields,
or introducing special Machine messages would cross that constraint.

## Selected route

Keep creation, guard callbacks, admission and ownership of a candidate inside
the runtime implementation. Existing native artifacts continue to register one
baseline StepMethod using the unchanged envelope. A candidate is a disposable
process-local implementation derived from the canonical PortableProgram already
supplied at portable materialization. It never supplies new language meaning.

The existing portable staging call already carries program inventories, binding
inventories, selection and manifest bytes. `begin_staged_portable_resumable_unit`
retains a private projection of these inputs. `StagedUnit` itself still retains
admission identities and digests rather than the program bytes. This
route does not need to ask replaceable CodeObject accessors for additional
optimizer facts or change the staging call's native signature.

The accepted portable contract makes canonical program bytes executable
authority and native code a physical projection (60L section 1). This permits
investigating another projection of that same meaning. An arbitrary registered
native method, a legacy source-manifest entry without those bytes, or a program
whose exact baseline Frame layout cannot be reproduced remains baseline-only.
Descriptor identity or a digest alone is not enough to authorize replacement.

The first admitted subset is portable Block bodies with multiple PCs,
entry values, binds and simple literals. Global reads and nested Block creation
remain baseline-only: their generated shims depend on module-owned Globals and
materialization state which the runtime cannot silently substitute. This is an
optimization eligibility limit, not a language restriction. The public compiler
and arbitrary native methods retain their existing capabilities.

## Admission requirements

1. Reuse the canonical lowering and descriptor serializer. Reproduce the exact
   baseline descriptor bytes, PC numbering, slot coloring, operand allocation
   order, roots and edge plans. Decline programs the internal backend cannot
   reproduce; do not change their registration or baseline behavior.
2. Reuse the existing native compiler implementation without importing the
   TCC module's singleton IdApi state or adding its exports to the Id floor.
   Extract the embedded compiler from the TCC language module into a shared
   Rust component, retaining unchanged exports, linking and cold-bootstrap
   behavior.
3. Compile only from admitted immutable inputs. Compiler setup and diagnostics
   must not send extra language messages, allocate extra Birnam operands, or
   invoke replaceable accessors. Failure must retain ordinary execution.
4. Retain the exact baseline descriptor allocation and separately own candidate
   executable memory. Selection follows resume-token allocation. A selected
   entry keeps its executable owner until native return, even if a callback
   invalidates or retires it. Cache eviction must not retire the active baseline
   generation or leak candidate code through dead descriptors.
5. Reuse 74F/74G's same-Frame recovery at PC boundaries. Per-access guards remain
   necessary inside a native activation because an allocation or callback can
   change lookup, registration or Frame contents after entry selection. A GC
   invalidation signal, if used, remains private runtime state and fails closed
   on saturation.
6. Keep all generated operations expressible as their original Id sends.
   Changing lookup, methods, inheritance or receiver vtables must preserve the
   original send's effects. Active old Frames retain old bodies; later sends
   see current bindings. No compiler cache becomes dispatch authority.

## Required evidence

Before normal admission, exercise a real portable materialization through the
unchanged native envelope, prove candidate entry independently of answers, and
repeat the existing mutation, precise-GC, same-Frame and native-retirement
matrix. Include failed compilation, incompatible descriptors, unsupported
programs, nested entry, candidate eviction on the native stack, and baseline
generation replacement while an old Frame remains active.

Compare ordinary release prefixes with instrumentation absent, measure both
steady execution and compilation/retention cost, and retain the existing host
gates and spread criterion. An implementation that merely passes the fixture
does not establish a usable production tier or a performance benefit.

## Prefix measurement protocol

Before the first comparison run, fix seven groups of three normal release
prefixes: `5e242e70`, the preserved 74J build, and the combined 74J/74K build.
Rotate and reverse their execution order. Run the same portable materialization
fixture at 1,024 and 4,096 iterations, with one cold call, 32 warmup calls and
five repetitions per process. Record materialization, first-call and warmup
cost separately. After the canonical phase, change the program's called method
and install the real native forwarding lookup from 74J; measure five fallback
repetitions and verify changed answers and post-eviction/GC behavior.

Include the unchanged ordinary-send control at 100,000 iterations. Use the
existing host preflight and interval gates. For each pair of variants and each
warm/fallback/control row, require the median difference to exceed both observed
sample ranges before classifying improvement or regression. Any such regression
prevents promotion. Retain all samples and rejected attempts. This new portable
fixture does not replace or retroactively qualify 74J's longer E1 protocol.

The runner verifies candidate source/prefix identity and compares historical
baseline/74J floor binaries with the preserved receipts. All three floor export
inventories and the frozen API, registration, descriptor and image authorities
must agree. No instrumentation is compiled into timed prefixes.

## Implemented admission and recovery

`runtime/native_tier.rs` derives candidates from the existing portable staging
inputs. It uses the canonical lowerer, slot coloring, descriptor serializer and
per-PC emitter. Registration admits a candidate only when the reproduced
descriptor bytes and PC count exactly match the accepted baseline. The existing
native registration envelope and all its validation remain unchanged.

The private registry holds weak descriptor identities, bounded to 256 records.
Eligible bodies have 2–4,096 PCs and at most 256 KiB of generated C. Native
compilation waits for 64 StepMethod entries. The shared
`birnam-native-compiler` crate owns a relocated libtcc unit independently of the
TCC language module. Its private functions add no floor exports or IdApi state.
Failed compilation and ineligible inputs retain baseline execution.

The driver allocates the original resume token before selection. Candidate
entries omit token decoding and the PC switch; all generated body sends, operand
boxes and allocation order remain unchanged. There is no repeated-read cache.
The exact descriptor allocation, active Frame and baseline generation stay
authoritative. Mutation, guard failure or eviction withdraws the candidate and
the next PC resumes through that Frame's original baseline. Each native entry
retains its executable owner until return, including during GC, nested entry
and cache eviction.

Twelve paired cases pass in debug and release: canonical execution, method
mutation, custom lookup, private Machine receiver, precise GC, eviction while
native code is active, saturated epochs, active body replacement, nested entry,
failed compilation, incompatible descriptor bytes and aborted publication.
Independent native-entry and baseline-decoding observations prove selection
and recovery. Old active Frames keep their bodies; a later send sees replacement.
The ordinary installed-prefix fixture also verifies portable materialization,
CodeObject identity, changed answers, materialization eviction and GC.

The [verification receipt](../measurements/74k-verification.json) records the
full workspace, native-prefix, cold-archive and relocation gates. The floor's
25 exports and the TCC module's exports, install name and dependencies agree
with the prior contract.

## Measurement result

The [retained measurement](../measurements/74k-runtime-owned-native-tier.json)
contains all seven host-gated groups, source and prefix hashes, raw outputs and
setup costs. All fifteen warm, fallback and control comparisons are within the
observed ranges. The following medians are microseconds per timed repetition:

| Work | Original baseline | 74J | 74J + 74K |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Warm, 1,024 iterations | 41,526 | 35,692 | 35,984 |
| Fallback, 1,024 iterations | 44,794 | 45,758 | 44,848 |
| Warm, 4,096 iterations | 217,929 | 188,269 | 187,917 |
| Fallback, 4,096 iterations | 219,816 | 220,139 | 227,930 |
| Ordinary-send control | 4,702,572 | 4,233,125 | 4,212,310 |

These medians do not establish improvement or regression under the declared
criterion. Embedding the compiler increases the floor from 731,952 bytes in
74J to 1,334,576 bytes, a 602,624-byte cost. This revision establishes native-tier
admission and same-Frame recovery under the existing interfaces; its timing
does not justify a PC-specialization performance claim. 74H read caching remains
an experiment. Further dispatch optimization is measured separately in
[74L](74l-guarded-default-lookup.md).
close_reason: Runtime-owned native admission and same-Frame recovery implemented through unchanged portable staging and registration. Twelve paired debug/release cases and full-prefix gates pass; combined candidate qualifies in 74L, without an independent PC-specialization speedup claim.

title: Optimize canonical metacircular lookup with guarded fallback (Design 74L)
description:
# 74L — Guard the existing default lookup implementation

Status: implemented and correctness-verified, 2026-09-11. The combined 74J/74K/74L
candidate meets the declared timing criterion against the original baseline
on the 1,024-iteration warm fixture, without an above-spread regression. The
incremental 74L comparisons are inconclusive. The protocol below preceded implementation and measurement.
The 74K three-prefix comparison completed with every row inside its observed
spread. No independent speedup is claimed for PC specialization.

## Problem and change

Even an ordinary send using the canonical lookup primitive recursively sends
`lookup` through the metacircular resolver. 74J eliminates this work for
canonical Machine slot sends, but other sends still pay it. Optimize the
default lookup *implementation* while preserving every semantic lookup.

After the existing metacircular base case, and only while a surrounding
dispatch-read lease is active, check that the receiver's vtable uses the
canonical metavtable, that the canonical metavtable uses itself, and that its
direct `lookup` entry is the actual floor lookup function. Check resumable
registration independently of dictionary mutation. A registered lookup carrier,
custom lookup or private metavtable must retain ordinary resolution and effects.

When eligible, run the same private dictionary lookup used by that canonical
primitive. Resolve the current dictionary every time: do not cache method
targets, results, receiver values or native-code ownership. Keep ordinary
resolve-and-pin classification, invocation and DNU handling after lookup.
The outer dispatch-read lease still fences retirement. At a saturated mutation
epoch, recheck the cached root conditions on every call.

This changes neither the IdApi table nor any exported native interface, language
selector, primitive meaning, Frame layout, registration record or image format.
Each result remains expressible by the original ordinary Id send. In particular,
an effectful custom lookup cannot be skipped or called an extra time.

## Acceptance

Compare enabled/disabled lookup in fresh runtimes. Prove hits independently of
answers; cover native replacement, inheritance, shadowing/removal, DNU arguments,
private metavtables, custom lookup, saturation and resumable lookup registration
whose address still equals the floor function. Retain the prior real native
mutation, same-Frame, precise-GC, native-retirement and full-prefix gates.

Reuse 74K's fixed portable benchmark, sizes, seven groups, warmup, forwarding
lookup fallback, ordinary-send control, host gates and spread criterion. Compare
the preserved 74K prefix with the updated candidate and the original baseline.
This is a new implementation revision, not a reinterpretation of 74K's results.
Record code-size and setup cost alongside steady execution. Any above-spread
candidate regression prevents promotion; no gain is claimed from a result within
the observed spread.

## Implementation and verification

`Runtime::bind_active` retains its existing metacircular base case, then checks
the private `guarded_default_lookup_eligible` predicate. A hit calls the same
`lookup_method_active` implementation as the canonical primitive. A miss follows
the existing lookup send. The cached value covers only the canonical root
conditions at a dictionary epoch; every target lookup still reads the current
dictionary and inheritance chain. Receiver metavtable identity and resumable
registration are checked independently on each attempt.

Two focused tests pass in debug and release. Eight enabled/disabled cases cover
canonical dispatch, method replacement, inheritance changes, shadow removal,
global lookup override, a private metavtable, epoch saturation and missing-method
argument forwarding. Lookup effects and original argument identities agree;
guard hits are observed independently. A separate test registers the canonical
lookup function address as a resumable carrier without mutating the dictionary,
checks invalidation and restoration, and proves that the published carrier
actually handles the next lookup.

The complete Id suite passes with 131 tests and seven existing ignored tests.
The [full verification receipt](../measurements/74l-verification.json) records
workspace tests, normal native prefixes, independent cold archives and relocated
runtimes. The timing runner additionally reruns all twelve native-tier pairs in
debug and release before measuring the uninstrumented prefixes.
The final 74F/74G/74H recovery and native-unload runners pass in both profiles;
74I's twelve fresh C-client processes agree against ordinary debug/release floor
builds. The three guarded Machine tests also pass in release. Their receipts
and source hashes are linked from the final verification receipt.

Run the bounded correctness checks with `mise run native-tier-test`. Reproduce
the three-prefix comparison using `scripts/runtime-native-tier.py --design 74L`
with explicit `--baseline`, `--slots` and `--candidate` prefixes. Here `--slots`
names the preserved 74J/74K prefix; the receipt records these labels explicitly.
Use a distinct `--output` for every new measurement attempt.

## Measurement result and limits

The [retained receipt](../measurements/74l-guarded-default-lookup.json) contains
all seven groups of process medians and setup costs, prefix/source hashes and
interval samples. Every host gate passed, with median idle CPU of 66.54–70.16%
and no low-idle intervals. The candidate matches the current source manifest;
all three floor export inventories contain the same 25 symbols. The API,
registration, descriptor, ordinary emitter and image authorities are unchanged.

Times below are microseconds; warm/fallback values are medians of seven
fresh-process medians, each using five timed repetitions:

| Work | Original baseline | 74J + 74K | 74J + 74K + 74L | Candidate vs original |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Warm, 1,024 iterations | 42,698 | 37,129 | 35,322 | 17.3% improvement, qualified |
| Fallback, 1,024 iterations | 44,533 | 45,501 | 44,719 | Inconclusive |
| Warm, 4,096 iterations | 213,785 | 198,123 | 189,363 | Inconclusive |
| Fallback, 4,096 iterations | 213,075 | 222,010 | 221,921 | Inconclusive |
| Ordinary-send control | 4,793,237 | 4,546,193 | 4,387,164 | Inconclusive |

For the qualified row, the median improvement is 7,376 us, exceeding both
observed ranges (4,041 and 4,720 us). There is no above-spread candidate
regression. All five incremental comparisons against the 74J/74K prefix remain
within variation. The 74J/74K prefix also improves against the original baseline
on the smaller warm fixture in this run. Consequently the evidence qualifies
the combined candidate, but does not isolate a benefit attributable to 74L or
PC specialization. It neither changes 74K's earlier inconclusive result nor
qualifies 74J's rejected longer E1 measurements.

For 1,024 iterations, median materialization cost is 591/688/701 us across the
three prefixes; first-call cost is 19/19/19 us, and the 32-call warmup costs
1,284/1,662/1,594 us. At 4,096 iterations those setup medians are 565/599/609 us,
18/19/18 us and 1,240/1,465/1,410 us. The native-tier compilation occurs during
warmup. These are reported costs, without a separate significance claim.

The final floor library is 1,334,464 bytes, 112 bytes smaller than 74J/74K and
602,704 bytes larger than the original baseline. The added compiler and native
ownership mechanism are a real footprint cost. The implemented tier covers
eligible portable Blocks and same-Frame recovery at existing PC boundaries;
inlining, unboxing, repeated-read caching and multicore execution remain outside
this promotion.
close_reason: Guarded canonical lookup implemented; current dictionaries and custom/native/resumable effects preserved. Full and focused regressions pass. Seven controlled groups qualify the combined candidate at 17.3% on the smaller warm fixture, with no above-spread regression; incremental lookup gain remains inconclusive.

title: Isolate native-tier performance, coverage and costs (Design 74M)
description:
# 74M — Isolate native-tier performance and coverage

Status: completed, 2026-09-11. Seven controlled on/off groups show no qualified
steady-execution or whole-process memory benefit. The smaller chain's warmup
regresses by 420 us. Separate diagnostics prove limited coverage and candidate
withdrawal on unrelated symbol interning. Production source remains fixed at
`24e200a3`; no optimizer expansion or public API/ABI/semantic change was made.
The protocol and diagnostic amendment below preceded the timing comparisons;
their original text is preserved in the measurement receipt.

## Question

74L qualified the combined implementation on one warm portable fixture. Its
separate native-tier and lookup gains were inconclusive. Determine whether the
native tier itself earns its compilation, retention and footprint costs, and
whether representative ordinary work reaches it.

## Isolation

Build ordinary release prefixes from the same committed source. The enabled
variant is unchanged. In an isolated source snapshot, the disabled variant
empties only native-tier staging and selection; 74J Machine sends, 74L lookup,
baseline compilation, registration and execution remain identical. Retain the
exact patch, source/prefix manifests and floor exports. Compare other installed
binaries to expose any build differences. No development helper ABI is added.
Common registration bookkeeping, including descriptor copying, stays in both
variants. This isolates the optional staging/compilation/selection work rather
than reconstructing a pre-74K runtime. Both snapshots receive identical hashed
prebuilt terminal-wrapper inputs required by the normal source-build manifest.

During preparation, normal rebuilding changed temporary `LC_ID_DYLIB` paths in
native and stage1 library headers. For timing, compose three experiment prefixes
from the enabled prefix's identical host/module files, replacing only the floor
with each variant's release-built floor. Assert that every other binary is
byte-identical. Keep the original build receipts separately; remove the canonical
install receipt from each composed prefix and label its exact composition.
These are explicit experiment prefixes, not a new packaged-runtime publication.

A third isolated snapshot adds private native-tier counters and clocks. Run it
separately for coverage and compilation diagnostics; never use its execution
times as performance samples. Record staging attempts, considered/eligible rows,
descriptor matches, selection attempts, native entries, invalidations, compiler
attempts/failures, compilation time, generated C bytes and live/peak native units.
Counters allocate no Birnam objects and send no language messages. Generated C
bytes are a source-size metric, not executable-memory accounting.

## Workloads and fixed protocol

Run six fresh-process scenarios for seven enabled/disabled pairs, alternating
order. Use five timed repetitions per scenario. Retain each new-workload
repetition and the existing portable-chain fixture's process medians.

- Existing portable-chain fixture at 1,024 and 4,096 iterations, including cold
  materialization, 32 warmup calls, method mutation, native forwarding lookup,
  post-eviction execution and GC. Preserve its existing process-median output.
- Ordinary compiler/evaluation: 32 compilations/evaluations of a small collection
  program per repetition, with checked answers.
- Ordinary collections: 32 collect/select pipelines over 256 values per
  repetition, with ordinary callback Blocks and checked answers.
- Portable collections: the same pipeline through an explicitly materialized
  multi-PC portable Block; callbacks are arguments and collection implementations
  remain ordinary. Record cold materialization and 32 warmup calls separately.
- Cold portable materialization: 64 cache-evict/materialize/call cycles per
  repetition. Each new native baseline gets one call, below the tier threshold.

New warm workloads receive 32 calls of warmup; cold materialization receives no
warmup. Workload syntax and answer checks may be repaired during untimed smoke
validation. Freeze hashes and all counts before the first performance pair.

Use the existing host preflight and interval gates unchanged. Complete all
builds/diagnostics before timing and run no parallel workload during measurement.
Record wall time and macOS maximum resident-set size for each process, plus
floor file size and separately measured tier compilation/retention diagnostics.
RSS is whole-process peak memory, not a direct measurement of JIT code size.

For each timed row, compare the median of seven process medians. Classify a
change only when its magnitude exceeds both observed process ranges. Apply the
same descriptive rule to wall time and peak RSS. Keep cold/setup costs separate
from steady execution. Preserve rejected attempts; do not tune workloads or
thresholds after seeing comparative timing. An above-spread regression prevents
a benefit claim for the tier on that workload. No overall speedup is inferred
from a single case or from diagnostic counters.

## Deliverable

Retain the reproducible runner, source-only snapshot patches, correctness
outputs, coverage/compilation diagnostics, all timing/host/memory samples and a
decision about the next bounded optimization. Ineligible ordinary programs are
a coverage result, not evidence that native code ran or a reason to change
language semantics. Existing Id malleability and same-Frame recovery remain the
required boundary for any subsequent implementation.

## Diagnostic amendment before the first timing pair

The initial three diagnostic repetitions found only 36 native PC entries in
each existing chain process and 33 in each portable-collection process, followed
by one invalidation. Those counts fit entirely within the 32-call warmup.
Ordinary evaluation/collections had zero native entries. All 320 cold
materializations per process were eligible but remained below the hot threshold.
The initial diagnostic receipt is retained separately; its clocks are diagnostic
only and some collection overlapped separate test compilation.

Retain all six scenarios and add a seventh, `steady-chain`, to answer the
otherwise-unmeasured steady-execution question. Create the batch/timing/result
closures and cells before portable admission; exercise that exact harness on
the synchronous Block first. Replace its target cell with the portable Block,
warm it with five 4,096-call batches, then measure another five such batches.
Print results only afterward. No runtime policy changes are made.

The instrumented smoke observed 122,817 native PC entries in this case. Its
portable warmup can account for at most 61,440 entries, so native execution
necessarily extends into the measured batches. Require at least 120,000 native
entries in each of the three final diagnostic repetitions before starting
timing. The extra scenario and this check precede all on/off timing comparisons;
the seven-pair host gates and classification rules are unchanged.

## Results

The [measurement receipt](../measurements/74m-native-tier-focus.json) contains all
seven controlled pairs, three diagnostic repetitions per scenario, exact
snapshot patches, build receipts, source hashes, composed-prefix binary hashes,
raw program output, resource usage and host samples. All host gates passed:
median idle CPU was 54.95–70.20%, with at most one low-idle sample per group.
Every timed binary except `libbirnam_id.dylib` is byte-identical across variants;
both floor export inventories have the same 25 symbols. Timed prefixes contain
no counters or diagnostic clocks.

Median batch times, in milliseconds, follow. Every row is inconclusive under
the predeclared spread criterion:

| Work | Tier disabled | Tier enabled | Enabled time change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original chain, 1,024 calls | 36.923 | 37.758 | +2.3% |
| Original chain, 4,096 calls | 203.800 | 195.918 | -3.9% |
| Compile/evaluate, 32 programs | 22.227 | 21.614 | -2.8% |
| Ordinary collections, 32 pipelines | 363.877 | 379.399 | +4.3% |
| Portable collections, 32 pipelines | 357.704 | 363.722 | +1.7% |
| Cold materialization, 64 cycles | 37.541 | 39.381 | +4.9% |
| Sustained native chain, 4,096 calls | 182.937 | 174.755 | -4.5% |

The sustained-native median saves 8.182 ms, below the observed process ranges
of 14.281 and 13.207 ms, so it does not establish a speedup. Both forwarding
lookup fallback comparisons, every whole-process wall-time comparison and
every peak-RSS comparison are also inconclusive. The apparent differences in
those medians must not be reported as improvements or regressions.

One setup cost *is* distinguishable: the original 1,024-call chain's 32-call
warmup takes 1.116 ms disabled versus 1.536 ms enabled. The 420 us increase
(37.6%) exceeds both ranges, 70 and 173 us. This is a warmup regression, not a
37.6% whole-program slowdown. Other setup/first-call comparisons are inconclusive.

## Coverage, compilation and memory

All three final diagnostic repetitions agree on the following counts. Counts
cover the entire process, including startup, and PC entries are not CPU-time
shares or a count of all language sends.

| Scenario | Eligible/considered portable rows | Native compilations | Native PC entries |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original chain, either size | 1/7 | 1 | 36 |
| Compile/evaluate | 0/4 | 0 | 0 |
| Ordinary collections | 0/4 | 0 | 0 |
| Portable collections | 1/5 | 1 | 33 |
| Cold materialization | 320/324 | 0 | 0 |
| Sustained native chain | 1/5 | 1 | 122,817 |

The original chain's 36 entries and portable collection's 33 entries are fully
accounted for by their warmups, followed by one invalidation. The added sustained
case uses the same precreated harness and retains native execution throughout
both portable warmup and timed batches. Its final invalidation occurs after
those batches. All compiler attempts succeed. Diagnostic native compilation
clocks range from 0.493 to 1.413 ms; these instrumented clocks are descriptive,
not a timing comparison with disabled execution.

Cold materialization emits 1,825,280 bytes of candidate C across 320 eligible
rows, spending 11.6–12.6 ms in private staging/preparation, yet compiles no native
candidate because each baseline gets only one call. This identifies optional
eager work that never pays off in this workload. C-source bytes are not JIT
executable bytes or retained-memory measurements.

Hot scenarios peak at one live candidate unit and finish with zero; the others
never allocate a candidate unit. Enabled/disabled floor files are 1,334,464 and
753,376 bytes respectively: this isolated tier costs 581,088 file bytes. This
differs from 74L's approximately 603 KB comparison against the older `5e242e70`
baseline because the disabled 74M build retains common registration bookkeeping
and the newer dispatch implementation. Whole-process peak RSS is noisy; none
of the measured RSS differences exceeds both observed ranges.

## Causal invalidation follow-up

After completing timing, the [symbol probe](../measurements/74m-native-tier-symbol-invalidation.json)
repeats the sustained harness with one send between portable warmup and the
final batches. Interning existing `oopAt:` retains 122,817 native entries.
Interning a previously unseen symbol leaves only 61,377 entries, all from the
portable warmup. Answers remain correct, and both runs compile exactly once.
The probe compares counts and answers only; its instrumented times are unused.

The source explains this behavior: inserting an interned symbol updates an
internal opaque dictionary via `add_weak_opaque_binding`, which increments the
same global vtable epoch used by native-tier selection. On any epoch difference,
selection permanently disables an already-compiled candidate without first
revalidating its actual assumptions. This demonstrates an unrelated-symbol
trigger; it does not claim to identify every mutation in the original harness.

## Decision and next bounded work

The native tier's independent performance case remains unproven. 74L's combined
17.3% result remains valid for that comparison, but is not evidence that native
PC specialization provided a steady-execution gain.

The next proposed implementation slice is to revalidate the candidate's actual
dependencies after unrelated dictionary changes while preserving fallback for
real Machine/lookup changes, descriptor identity, same-Frame continuation and
native ownership. A new interned symbol should no longer permanently discard
an otherwise-valid candidate. Then repeat this exact on/off comparison before
claiming a benefit. This proposal is tracked as `birnam-native-tier-revalidation-7qd`.
Separately, defer candidate C generation for cold bodies
until they approach admission; the cold-materialization diagnostics justify
investigating that work. Wider program eligibility and more complex optimization
remain subsequent choices based on measured payoff.

## Reproduction and verification

From a prepared macOS checkout with its normal terminal-wrapper build inputs
and no `BIRNAM_*` or `DYLD_*` runtime overrides (none were set for this run):

```sh
python3 scripts/native-tier-focus.py --work-dir /tmp/birnam-74m-new \
  --prepare --diagnose --measure --output /tmp/birnam-74m-new.json
python3 scripts/native-tier-invalidation-probe.py \
  --profile-prefix /tmp/birnam-74m-new/run-profile \
  --output /tmp/birnam-74m-symbol-new.json
```

An existing matching release prefix can be supplied with `--on-prefix` to avoid
rebuilding it. Use fresh work/output paths for each attempt. The five guarded
Machine/lookup tests pass in both debug and release in the disabled snapshot.
`mise run native-tier-test` passes against the unchanged production source.
All seven product scenarios pass their answer/identity/mutation/GC checks in
both timed variants. The [verification record](../measurements/74m-native-tier-verification.json)
links the exact evidence and archives the initial diagnostic runner, whose
source preceded the seventh-scenario amendment.
close_reason: Completed seven controlled on/off pairs with byte-identical host/modules, 21 final diagnostics and a causal symbol-invalidation probe. No independent speedup or RSS change qualified; smaller-chain warmup regressed 420 us. Correctness passes, production runtime is unchanged, and precise revalidation is recorded as proposed follow-up birnam-native-tier-revalidation-7qd.

title: Revalidate native-tier dependencies after unrelated dictionary changes
description:
# 74N — Revalidate native-tier dependencies

Status: completed, 2026-09-11. Correctness and increased native coverage are
verified. Seven controlled timing groups show no independent execution or memory
benefit beyond variation; both chain warmups regress relative to the disabled tier.
Tracker: `birnam-native-tier-revalidation-7qd`.

## Problem and change

74M proved that interning an unrelated symbol permanently withdraws a warmed
candidate. Its global dictionary epoch changes, although the candidate's actual
assumptions still hold. Native PC specialization retains the original body and
descriptor, and performs ordinary Id sends; it does not cache ordinary method
targets or language values.

Remove the candidate's saved epoch and its blanket epoch-difference rejection.
On every admission, retain exact descriptor allocation identity, the saturation
check, and `guarded_slot_access_eligible`. That guard already revalidates canonical
Machine read/write and lookup bindings after dictionary mutation, while checking
the actual Machine header and resumable registration independently on every
attempt. Its cached verdict is private and non-effectful. An actual dependency
failure still withdraws the candidate permanently, with same-Frame baseline
continuation and the selected activation's independent native-code owner.

Replacing an ordinary method, including the active body's published binding,
need not withdraw the candidate: an old Frame keeps its descriptor and body;
later sends resolve the current binding. No cached send targets are introduced.
New symbol and export activity should retain native admission. Saturated epochs
remain baseline-only. No IdApi, ABI, primitive semantics, descriptor, registration,
image format, eligible program subset, allocation order or hot threshold changes.
Eager candidate preparation remains as before; lazy preparation is separate work.

## Verification and fixed performance protocol

Extend the existing paired native/baseline checks with symbol insertion, export,
ordinary target replacement and registration without a dictionary mutation.
Retain the existing mutation, custom lookup, private Machine, saturation, exact
descriptor, nested entry, GC, active replacement and eviction/lifetime checks.
Run debug and release correctness plus the ordinary production verification gate.

Repeat all seven 74M scenarios unchanged, with seven alternating off/on groups,
five repetitions per process and the existing host preflight/interval gates.
Use the same median-difference criterion: a classified change must exceed both
observed process ranges. Report setup, execution, wall time and peak RSS separately.
Finish compilation and private diagnostic runs before timing. Do not tune counts,
workloads or thresholds after observing comparative results.

Archive committed `24e200a3` plus an explicit patch containing only this slice's
Rust changes. Build enabled, disabled and private-profile release variants from
that identical candidate snapshot. Reuse the 74M staging/selection disable and
private instrumentation transforms; compose prefixes with identical other
binaries and retain complete build manifests, patches and export inventories.
Keep 74M scripts and receipts intact. The new runner records its own source and
the imported 74M helpers and benchmark hashes. Strip runtime and host-gate
environment overrides for the experiment.

Run three separate diagnostic repetitions for coverage, compilation and native
unit retention. Require at least 120,000 native entries in each steady-chain
diagnostic. Repeat the existing/new-symbol probe; both must retain at least the
original 122,817 warm-plus-measured native entries and correct answers. Diagnostic
clocks are not comparative timing samples. A correctness pass or increased native
coverage alone does not establish a performance benefit.

## Correctness and coverage results

All eighteen native/baseline pairs pass in debug and release, including the six
new symbol/export/current-target and registration cases. The active replacement
case now keeps all three old-Frame PCs native, still returning the old answer
28 before a later send returns the replacement's 99. A separately replaced
terminal target returns 99 during the current invocation, proving sends remain
late-bound. Real Machine/lookup changes, saturation and eviction still fall back
without repeating effects. Registration at each canonical read/write/lookup
address vetoes admission without moving the dictionary epoch; removing that
unpublished registration does not resurrect the withdrawn candidate.

The five guarded Machine/lookup tests pass in debug and release in both normal
and disabled snapshots. `mise run verify` passes: 448 workspace tests pass,
11 remain ignored, and native-prefix, lifecycle, cold-archive and relocation
checks succeed. The public compatibility authorities remain byte-identical to
`24e200a3`, and all three floor variants expose the same 25 symbols.

All three separate diagnostic repetitions agree on these entry counts:

| Scenario | 74M native PC entries | 74N native PC entries |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Original chain, 1,024 calls | 36 | 15,399 |
| Original chain, 4,096 calls | 36 | 61,479 |
| Compile/evaluate | 0 | 0 |
| Ordinary collections | 0 | 0 |
| Portable collections | 33 | 513 |
| Cold materialization | 0 | 0 |
| Sustained native chain | 122,817 | 122,820 |

Both existing/new-symbol probes retain 122,820 entries, one successful native
compilation and correct answers. The three additional sustained entries are the
fixture's final post-measurement invocation. The original chain still withdraws
its candidate after the later custom-lookup installation. No ordinary program
became newly eligible: compile/evaluate and ordinary collections still never
enter this tier.

Hot scenarios peak at one native unit. Portable collections and the sustained
chain now retain that unit at the exit-profile callback, while their descriptors
remain live; original-chain scenarios end with zero after actual invalidation.
The retention is expected from preserving valid candidates. Diagnostic compilation
clocks range from 0.323 to 0.660 ms. Cold materialization still prepares 320 unused
candidates, emits 1,825,280 source bytes and never compiles a candidate; private
preparation clocks total 6.88–7.02 ms per process. These instrumented clocks are
descriptive and are not timing comparisons with 74M.

Enabled/disabled floor files are 1,334,256 and 753,376 bytes: 580,880 additional
file bytes. Generated source size and file size are not executable-memory usage;
whole-process peak RSS is measured separately in the timed comparison.

## Controlled timing results

The [preparation receipt](../measurements/74n-native-tier-preparation.json) retains
the complete candidate patch, build/composition manifests, debug/release paired
tests, all 21 diagnostics and both symbol probes. The
[verification receipt](../measurements/74n-native-tier-verification.json) retains
the production gate output, both disabled-variant guard test outputs, source
parity checks and the authorized process-pause/resume record. The
[completed timing receipt](../measurements/74n-native-tier-focus.json) retains
all seven groups, individual samples, process medians, resource usage and host
checks. Its source hashes and candidate build are identical to preparation.

Every preflight and interval gate passed. Median idle CPU during groups was
71.22–73.45%, with zero low-idle intervals. With explicit user approval, `rk` was
paused for the whole comparison, equally for both variants, and resumed after
approximately 177 seconds. Its original process identity and running state were
verified afterward; the fallback resume watchdog did not fire. No build or
diagnostic workload overlapped timing, and no threshold or workload changed.

Batch results in milliseconds follow. Range width is maximum minus minimum
across the seven process medians. Every row is inconclusive under the declared
criterion, which requires the median difference to exceed **both** widths:

| Work | Disabled median | Enabled median | Disabled range width | Enabled range width |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original chain, 1,024 calls | 36.168 | 36.145 | 3.031 | 3.945 |
| Original chain, 4,096 calls | 194.545 | 184.686 | 17.088 | 18.168 |
| Forwarding lookup fallback, 1,024 calls | 45.654 | 44.858 | 4.946 | 3.649 |
| Forwarding lookup fallback, 4,096 calls | 220.947 | 222.933 | 8.339 | 18.933 |
| Compile/evaluate, 32 programs | 21.918 | 21.804 | 2.292 | 2.665 |
| Ordinary collections, 32 pipelines | 352.759 | 350.579 | 35.384 | 30.719 |
| Portable collections, 32 pipelines | 344.960 | 352.843 | 49.200 | 21.772 |
| Cold materialization, 64 cycles | 37.025 | 38.885 | 1.808 | 2.502 |
| Sustained native chain, 4,096 calls | 174.779 | 172.023 | 16.522 | 19.886 |

The larger original chain's apparent 5.1% saving and sustained chain's apparent
1.6% saving are below variation; neither establishes a speedup. Cold
materialization's apparent 5.0% increase also remains inconclusive. All
whole-process wall-time and peak-RSS comparisons are inconclusive, including
the scenarios that now retain their native unit until process exit. Their full
individual samples are in the timing receipt; no memory improvement is claimed.
Whole-process medians and range widths are below, with disabled / enabled
values in each cell. RSS is peak resident memory for the whole process, not a
direct measure of native code allocation:

| Scenario | Wall median (ms) | Wall range width (ms) | Peak RSS median (MiB) | RSS range width (MiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| chain-1024 | 687.35 / 690.26 | 63.64 / 62.44 | 207.12 / 217.84 | 17.53 / 18.70 |
| chain-4096 | 2232.75 / 2216.82 | 54.61 / 40.59 | 223.66 / 226.50 | 40.22 / 25.08 |
| eval | 279.26 / 286.99 | 27.69 / 37.80 | 126.88 / 129.69 | 21.00 / 13.86 |
| collections | 2258.64 / 2235.16 | 53.08 / 222.94 | 221.58 / 237.33 | 31.67 / 23.67 |
| portable-collections | 2244.85 / 2253.48 | 175.06 / 179.62 | 221.38 / 222.59 | 38.09 / 16.95 |
| materialize-cold | 453.04 / 473.62 | 21.80 / 29.47 | 134.44 / 139.20 | 15.12 / 10.59 |
| steady-chain | 2631.37 / 2623.57 | 67.16 / 171.63 | 231.17 / 228.30 | 23.56 / 39.88 |

Two setup regressions exceed both observed widths:

| 32-call warmup | Disabled median (us) | Enabled median (us) | Increase (us) | Disabled / enabled range widths (us) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original 1,024-call scenario | 1,115 | 1,467 | 352 (31.6%) | 168 / 242 |
| Original 4,096-call scenario | 1,064 | 1,360 | 296 (27.8%) | 172 / 146 |

These are warmup costs relative to tier-disabled execution, not whole-program
slowdowns and not a direct comparison of the 74M and 74N implementations. The
other setup and first-call differences remain within observed variation.

## Rejected attempt and reproduction

The [first timing attempt](../measurements/74n-native-tier-rejected-1.json) did
not pass group 1's preflight and collected no comparative samples. The unchanged
gate requires the hottest competing process to use at most 80% of one core.
The unrelated `rk` daemon repeatedly exceeded that limit (the last captured
preflight reported 193.1%). After repeated rejections, the still-retrying
preflight was terminated; this was not its automatic 900-second timeout.
No host threshold was relaxed and no other application's process was paused
during that first attempt. The subsequent approved pause enabled the completed
run reported above; the rejected evidence remains intact.

Reuse the verified prefixes on a quiet host and write a new receipt for each
attempt:

```sh
python3 scripts/native-tier-revalidation.py --work-dir /tmp/birnam-74n-run \
  --measure --output /tmp/birnam-74n-run/timing-new.json
```

To reproduce everything in a fresh directory:

```sh
python3 scripts/native-tier-revalidation.py --work-dir /tmp/birnam-74n-new \
  --correctness --prepare --diagnose --probe \
  --output /tmp/birnam-74n-new/preparation.json
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=.cargo-target mise run verify
python3 scripts/native-tier-revalidation.py --work-dir /tmp/birnam-74n-new \
  --measure --output /tmp/birnam-74n-new/timing.json
```

Finish other build/test work before timing. The original 74M scripts, fixtures,
counts and receipts remain intact.

## Decision and next work

Dependency revalidation fixes premature withdrawal without weakening Id
malleability or changing the ABI. The implementation and focused testing task
are complete. Increased native coverage still does not establish an independent
performance benefit, and the reproducible warmup costs remain material.

The next bounded experiment should defer candidate preparation until a body is
hot enough to need it. Cold diagnostics already identify 320 candidate sources
prepared but never compiled per process. This removes optional eager work from
cold bodies without widening language restrictions or program eligibility; it
will still need the same correctness and cost comparison. Hot compilation's
warmup cost will remain a separate question. General inlining, read caching,
unboxing and broader program eligibility are not justified by these results.
