All 18 paired cases, five guarded tests in both profiles/variants, full production verification, 21 diagnostics, both symbol probes and seven controlled timing groups pass. rk was paused with explicit user approval and resumed with original identity verified. No independent execution or RSS benefit clears both sample ranges; warmups regress by 352 and 296 us. Complete results and pause/resume evidence are retained under Design 74N. Next proposed experiment: defer unused cold candidate preparation; not implemented.
close_reason: Dependency revalidation verified without ABI or semantic changes; seven controlled timing groups completed with approved rk pause and verified resume. Increased coverage, no qualified execution/RSS benefit, and 352/296 us warmup regressions documented with all samples and prior rejected attempt retained.

title: Assess deoptimization architectural fit with reconstruction and semantic counterexamples (74O)
description:
# 74O — Deoptimization architectural fit

Status: bounded feasibility experiments complete, 2026-09-11. General
reconstruction is test-only; no production admission or performance claim.

## Finding

Birnam's explicit Frames, compiler layouts, GC roots and generation ownership
can support a bounded reconstruction mechanism. Ordinary Birnam code can produce
the tested recovery policy, including after source-independent compilation.
These results justify designing a production recovery contract; they do not
justify treating a general optimizer as already supported.

There are fundamental conflicts with **specific optimizations**: replacing an
escaped identity, removing an observable native effect, exposing an absent Frame,
or delaying an allocation beyond an observable finalizer checkpoint changes the
program. Later reconstruction cannot repair an observation already made. These
are eligibility limits, not evidence that deoptimization itself requires a less
malleable language. Arbitrary opaque native activations also remain outside the
reconstructable state: call them with concrete state and preserve entry barriers.

One concrete implementation gap is V2 continuation action publication. Existing
continuation storage preserves reconstructed compiler Frames, including roots and
pending call transitions, but capture/suspend publication still calls the V1-only
`set_program_counter`. The experiment distinguishes these two paths; it does not
silently bypass the rejected public operation and call that production support.

## Scope and reproducibility

The user requested bounded experiments to determine deoptimization's broad fit
with core tenets, invariants and the current implementation. The predeclared
dimensions were logical call-chain reconstruction, observation/native boundaries,
object elimination/identity, and compiler/floor expressibility. The public IdApi,
Method ABI, primitive semantics and durable formats remain fixed. Internal
test-only extensions are permitted. Earlier uncommitted 74M/74N work is retained.

Run from the repository root on supported arm64 macOS:

```sh
python3 scripts/deopt-architectural-fit.py --verify
```

The [runner](../../scripts/deopt-architectural-fit.py) builds an ordinary disposable
prefix outside the source tree to execute the Id producer; it does not replace
the user's installation or install the test-only reconstruction helper. It
records exact commands, outputs, source hashes, generated portable programs,
compiler descriptors/C/facts, producer source/output and prefix binary hashes in
the [receipt](../measurements/74o-deoptimization-fit.json). Frozen ABI, image,
descriptor, registration and baseline emitter authorities are compared with
`24e200a3`. The full gate runs `mise run verify`.

Debug and release each pass five tests: 22 execution rows (nine expected-equal
pairs and two deliberate counterexample pairs), plus object and continuation
summaries. Both profiles produce identical recorded observations. Full gate:
453 Rust tests passed, 11 diagnostic tests ignored; native-prefix, cold-archive
and relocated-runtime gates passed.

No timing or speedup is inferred. These probes run under instrumented conditions,
with a deliberately restricted native prefix. They do not supersede 74M/74N's
inconclusive independent native-tier performance results.

## 1. Reconstructing an absent logical call

The [runtime experiment](../../rust/birnam-id/src/runtime/architectural_fit_experiment.rs)
encodes two portable Blocks, invokes the production lowering, liveness, coloring,
descriptor and baseline C generators, and compiles actual native code. Its caller
normally sends to a callee whose body keeps two aliases, observes them, and
returns twice their value.

The experimental candidate executes a bounded prefix with entry values, aliases,
and one explicitly trusted pure identity leaf. It then reconstructs the missing
callee at PC 1. The caller remains its original allocation with its existing
pending call. Recorded Frame depth goes from one to two. Ordinary baseline code
resumes through the unchanged real stackless driver, receives native answers and
commits the caller's original return destination. Recovery itself performs no Id
send, Birnam allocation or callback while installing state.

The [arena helper](../../rust/birnam-id/src/execution/inline_recovery_experiment.rs)
checks current caller/descriptor allocation, pending-call kind and return slot,
callee PC, physical slot bounds, source spill bounds, duplicate destinations and
explicit initialization of traced locations before mutation. Seven malformed
recipes are rejected: duplicate target, missing live locations, invalid source
spill, invalid destination, invalid callee PC, wrong return slot, and a different
caller descriptor allocation with the same public identity. Complete logical
arena snapshots include pending edges, root-state PCs, words, scratch contents,
return destinations, ownership entries and handles; all remain unchanged.

This is not a general metadata-admission validator. Descriptor/entry association
and spill provenance come from the trusted fixture/compiler. A production API
must validate its authority and acquire/release roots and code pins transactionally.
The experiment reconstructs one absent callee, not arbitrary-depth virtual call
chains, virtual closure environments or cyclic materialization graphs.

## 2. Observations and native participation

| Case | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Plain | Both executions return 28 with identical effects and Frame observations; only the candidate reconstructs. |
| GC | A precise root-provider callback writes boxed 22 into both aliased recovered locations. Both executions return 44; unrelated garbage is reclaimed. |
| Active replacement | Existing Frames finish in their original generation and return 28; a future send uses the replacement and returns 99. Registry retirement is refused while active; entries and pins release after completion. |
| Machine override | An override installed after recovery receives six calls in both executions. |
| Custom lookup | An override installed after recovery receives 26 calls in both executions. |
| Observable native identity | Candidate guard declines optimization; the arbitrary native method runs with its effect and correct callee Frame. |
| Native reentry | Nested stackless execution reaches depth three and returns correctly without disturbing the outer computation. |
| Native entry barrier | An actual nested drive rejects capture and suspension across its entry barrier, then both computations finish. |
| Bad maps | Seven rejections preserve live arena state; the subsequent valid recovery completes. |

Frame inspection uses ordinary Id `currentFrameView`, `generationIdentity` and
`programCounter` sends. The saved original caller stays usable across recovery;
saved views are stale after return. These observations include the existing
distinction between a public next PC and the root state of an in-progress call.

Two deliberately unsound controls are essential:

- Skipping an arbitrary native method that happens to return its receiver keeps
  the numeric answer but loses its effect and Frame observation.
- Calling that observer before reification keeps both answer and effect sequence,
  but the observer sees caller generation 74001 instead of callee generation 74002.

Thus arbitrary native methods need no new ABI or metadata to remain callable.
They cannot be assumed pure or be called with hidden logical state that they may
observe. The fixture's pure-leaf authority is explicit and test-owned. It retains
the exact installed method pointer; separately taking Rust function addresses
was insufficient in a release build and is not an identity contract.

Native code ownership in this new fixture is tested at registration/pin lifetime
boundaries. Its local Unit owners are deliberately retained until fixture cleanup.
Actual unloading is exercised by the existing generated-deoptimization regression
tests in the full gate, not newly demonstrated by this fixture's local Unit drop.

## 3. Object elimination and observable allocation

The object test sends the ordinary Id identity selector `==`:

- A fresh integer box with the same numeric value differs from an escaped box.
- Materializing once and supplying that Oop to both aliases preserves identity.
- Independently materializing each alias creates different identities.

The allocation control uses a legal native finalizer, including the String
storage cleanup it owns, and explicit precise collections. Retaining the
allocation produces one finalizer effect at the checkpoint. Eliminating it
produces zero. Materializing and collecting later reaches the same eventual
count but cannot change the earlier checkpoint. Keeping the allocation before
observation reproduces the baseline result.

These are runtime semantic counterexamples, not a production escape-analysis or
scalar-replacement implementation. Unescaped, unobserved virtual objects remain
possible candidates, provided a compiler can prove the relevant conditions and
materialize a shared identity before exposure. Cycles, mutable captured Cells,
raw storage and finalizer-bearing object virtualization are not implemented here.

There is a further legality obligation even for the prefix used in section 1:
it omits some baseline Machine operand-box allocations. The experiment does not
prove equivalence under every allocation-triggered collection schedule or every
GC observer. Production optimization must establish that omitted allocations
are unobservable, preserve required effects/checkpoints, or decline optimization.
A passing selected-checkpoint comparison is not permission to weaken allocation
or native-observation semantics.

## 4. Compiler policy and floor mechanism

The [Id-authored policy](../../scripts/fixtures/deopt-recovery-policy.birnam)
receives the actual production compiler's physical slot count, nil spill index,
and live `(physical slot, spill index)` facts. Using ordinary collections and
sends, it constructs all slot assignments. The runner executes the policy both
ordinarily and after `Codegen materializeResumable:` of its source-independent
CodeObject. Both produce the same recipe. Debug and release runtime probes then
consume those produced bytes as their actual recovery slot map; an independent
comparison checks the compiler's liveness/layout mapping.

This establishes that the bounded mapping policy and its data need not be
Rust-only. File transport is experimental. It does not establish an ordinary Id
operation for admitting generation capabilities, a complete self-hosted optimizing
compiler, or a production recovery ABI. Those remain concrete admission work.

| Responsibility | Existing support and required work |
| --- | --- |
| Compiler / Id policy | Choose legal speculation; identify observation checkpoints; compute logical calls, resume PCs, live values and shared identities. Existing lowering/layout facts and the Id recipe producer demonstrate a bounded part. General recovery-map generation and escape/effect analysis remain missing. |
| Optimized native entry | Keep live Oops rooted and original code owned; spill state and exit before an assumption-dependent observation. The bounded prefix has no callback/allocation while its callee is absent. General spill/root maps are not implemented. |
| Floor / Runtime mechanism | Validate recovery authority and install complete Frames without user callbacks midway; preserve pending calls, roots, aliases and generation ownership. The test-only installer and existing driver demonstrate the basic transfer. Production admission and multi-Frame atomicity remain missing. |
| Ordinary Id protocol | Describe policy/data through objects and sends, retaining malleability. The policy runs today; the checked reconstruction operation is not exposed today. An added guarded Machine operation is a possible design direction, not a shipped API. |
| Continuation mechanism | Existing storage/restore handles reconstructed V2 state and one-shot ownership. Action publication needs an explicit V2 transition contract. No serialization of opaque native activations is proposed. |

No additional IdApi table field is required by these experiments. That negative
ABI result alone does not prove a satisfactory final protocol; its authority,
override behavior and failure semantics must be designed and tested explicitly.

## 5. Continuation boundary experiment

A separate test constructs production V2 descriptors, stages a pending caller
call, and reconstructs the callee. It first proves that ordinary capture and suspension
publication return `InvalidProgramCounter` and leaves logical state unchanged.
It then tests the existing private continuation storage operation directly.

The stored segment contains both Frames. A precise collection with no native
stack scanning retains a value reachable through the detached V2 roots. Restore
preserves descriptor allocations, PCs, root-state PCs, pending edges, return
destinations, values and scratch state. Old Frame handles become stale, as
continuation capture already requires. A second restore is rejected as consumed.

This isolates a publication/integration gap from representational compatibility.
It is not a successful language-level suspend/resume journey, delayed reentry
through an arbitrary C activation, or a new pin/unload test. Supporting V2 capture
and suspension through normal compiler/Machine operations requires explicit
resume/result transition semantics, not simply deleting the V1 check.

## 6. Tenet assessment and next step

| Tenet / invariant | Classification supported by the experiments |
| --- | --- |
| Explicit stackless Frames and driver | Demonstrated compatibility for one reconstructed callee and original caller. General call-chain reconstruction is implementation work, not established by this test. |
| Full malleability and reflective state | Demonstrated at tested boundaries; speculation must stop or reify before arbitrary observation. Exposing absent state is a fundamental conflict for that optimization. |
| Native participation | Compatible with concrete call boundaries and existing barriers. Recovering an opaque native activation without its cooperation is outside the supported model. |
| Id expressibility | Bounded policy/data demonstrated through ordinary and source-independent Id compilation. Production admission and full compiler policy remain gaps. |
| Identity and aliases | Single materialization can preserve a virtual identity; replacing an already escaped identity or splitting aliases is fundamentally invalid. General materialization graphs remain untested. |
| GC and allocation effects | Recovered/detached roots survive precise GC and callback mutation in the probes. Erasing already observable allocation/finalizer effects is invalid; general allocation-elision eligibility remains unresolved. |
| Code-generation lifetime | Existing registration guards retain active generations through replacement; cleanup releases pins. Existing unload regressions cover actual native mapping retirement. |
| Suspension / continuations | V2 storage is compatible in the bounded test; normal V2 action publication is an implementation gap. Native barriers remain required. |
| Frozen ABI and durable formats | Authorities remain byte-for-byte unchanged; all new recovery access is test-only. No production transport is implied. |
| Concurrency / owner authority | Experiments stay on the existing owner thread. Deoptimization neither supplies concurrency nor requires changing that model; parallel safety is not qualified here. |
| Native speed | Unanswered by this feasibility work. Correct reconstruction does not establish worthwhile optimization or amortization. |

Proceed with a bounded **production recovery-contract design and implementation**
before adding general inlining or scalar replacement. It should admit an
Id-described recipe against owned compiler metadata, validate and transfer roots
and code pins atomically, and define the V2 continuation transition. Its first
consumer should use an optimization whose omitted observations are explicitly
proved safe. Retain the adverse cases here as admission criteria. Performance
testing follows that semantic gate; hotness/preparation tuning remains a separate
74N follow-up.

This assessment does not find a demonstrated need to sacrifice a core tenet for
deoptimization. It does find hard limits on optimizations that cross observable
identity/effect boundaries, and it leaves general-case eligibility and production
admission unproven. A bounded experiment cannot establish universal compatibility.

## Completion audit

| Predeclared requirement | Evidence / scope |
| --- | --- |
| Missing logical callee, production layouts, real driver, caller/return state | Section 1; nine paired matrix cases, depth counters and independent baseline execution. |
| Observation, native reentry, Machine/lookup, GC, capture barriers | Section 2; paired observations plus two deliberately wrong native controls. |
| Object identity, aliases, allocation/collection counterexamples | Section 3; real Id identity sends and explicit finalizer checkpoint comparisons. |
| Inspectable recovery data and Birnam-authored policy | Section 4; compiler facts, ordinary/portable producer outputs, consumed runtime recipe. |
| Invalid maps preserve prior state; code lifetime | Seven full-arena snapshot rejections, active-retirement/cleanup assertions, existing unload regressions in full verification. |
| Debug/release, source receipts, unchanged authorities, full gate | Linked measurement receipt and reproducible runner. |
| Responsibility map, tenet classification, broad recommendation | Sections 4–6 distinguish demonstrated fit, fundamental invalid cases, implementation gaps and unresolved generality. |

The feasibility investigation is complete within these stated bounds. The
unimplemented production mechanisms are findings and recommended future work,
not features this investigation claims to have delivered.

Receipt and tenet assessment distinguish demonstrated reconstruction/storage fit, semantic counterexamples, V2 publication gaps, and missing production admission.

title: Complete V2 suspension/capture and remove Frame layout V1 (60P)
description:
# 60P — Complete V2 control and retire Frame layout V1

Status: implemented and verified, 2026-09-11.

The user requested completion of V2 suspension/capture and removal of the old
Frame layout after 74O exposed the incomplete control paths. This authorizes
runtime implementation and migration of handwritten probes. Public IdApi and
Method ABIs, canonical descriptor-v2 bytes, image formats and language malleability
remain intact. Unrelated version-1 protocols are not Frame layout V1.

## Control contract

A suspension or capture yields a result-bearing invocation. It uses an existing
V2 Call edge: source/target PCs, result destination, parallel copies, clear map
and root maps already describe the state before and after the supplied answer.
No new serialized edge kind or compiler-specific selector recognition is needed.

Publication validates the delimiter and exact Call edge, then stages it without
committing. The visible PC is the successor; predecessor roots remain active.
A Machine microcode override may convert an already staged matching Call into
Suspend or Capture. Mismatched result slots, PCs and transitions are rejected
before mutation. Ordinary Id Machine operations expose these actions as
`suspendAt:continueAt:` and `captureAt:continueAt:`.

While suspended or detached, the old root state and pending edge retain values
needed by the transfer. Resume/restore supplies the result and commits the
parallel copies, clears and successor roots exactly once before invoking the
next StepMethod. Continuations preserve one-shot consumption, original code
ownership and existing native-entry barriers. No native C activation is captured.

V2 becomes the only Frame representation. Handwritten probes declare genuine
V2 layouts and edges, using conservative root maps where precision is irrelevant.
No runtime switch, compatibility interpreter or synthetic V1 transition path is
retained. Tests for unsupported raw Frame slots move to V2 bounds/root-map checks.

## Required validation

- Real driver suspension and capture/restore with compiler-produced V2 layouts,
  nontrivial copies/clears, changing root maps, and correct supplied answers.
- Ordinary Machine sends and overridden microcode retain their effects.
- GC while paused/detached; active-generation ownership and one-shot consumption.
- Invalid/mutated actions, wrong results/PCs, nested-entry barriers and failed
  restore leave the appropriate prior state intact.
- Migrate the V1 probes and retain the broader runtime, native-tier, reflective,
  continuation and generated-deoptimization regressions.
- Debug/release checks and the full production verification gate; record actual
  completion evidence here before claiming the implementation finished.

## Implementation notes

The compiler already emits result-bearing Call edges for ordinary sends. A
Machine `callSite:` override can publish the matching Suspend/Capture action
through the new ordinary methods, so no compiler selector recognition or new
serialized edge is necessary. The driver validates the returned action against
the exact pending result destination. Publication preflights action storage and
numeric capabilities before staging; resume checks epoch capacity before commit.

All handwritten descriptors now go through V2 validation. The broader release
run exposed probe function-address assumptions: identical inert functions were
folded together, and an identity helper could acquire distinct addresses across
codegen units. Test-only barriers and an out-of-line helper make those assumptions
explicit. The registration production code is byte-identical to `24e200a3`;
compatibility runners compare its production portion while allowing maintenance
of the trailing `cfg(test)` module. Other frozen files remain byte-identical,
and receipts continue recording whole-file hashes.

The focused checks cover four executions: actual compiler-generated code and a
cyclic-copy layout, each suspended and captured. They check ordinary Machine
publication, tampered result rejection, rejected publication without Frame
mutation, precise GC with native-stack scanning disabled, changing root maps,
parallel copies and clears, wrong-Machine restore without consumption, and
one-shot completion. Existing regression tests retain generation-pin and native
entry-barrier coverage. General deoptimization reconstruction admission remains
separate work; completing V2 does not implement general inlining or unboxing.

## Completion evidence

[60P receipt](../measurements/60p-v2-control.json) records commands, source hashes,
frozen-authority comparisons and the four matching debug/release executions.

- Focused debug: 2 tests, all four suspension/capture executions pass.
- Entire runtime crate in release: 139 passed, 7 diagnostic tests ignored.
- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=.cargo-target MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS="$PWD" mise run verify`:
  455 workspace tests passed, 11 diagnostic tests ignored; native-prefix,
  image/registration lifecycle, two clean archive builds and relocated execution
  all passed. The clean builds produced identical source/output closures.
- All eight compatibility runners import successfully; the authority comparison
  accepts test-only changes and rejects a production mutation.
- No Frame layout V1 constructor, constant, direct PC setter or raw-slot branch
  remains in the Rust runtime. Public ABI, descriptor encoding, image and compiler
  authorities remain unchanged. No source changes occurred during the final gate.

An earlier gate attempt correctly rejected concurrent source edits; only the
final frozen-source run is recorded as successful. The user installation and
remote repository have not been changed by this task.
close_reason: V2 control complete and Frame layout V1 removed. Four matching debug/release control executions; 139 release runtime tests and 455 workspace tests pass. Native-prefix, cold-archive and relocation gates pass. Evidence: docs/measurements/60p-v2-control.json.

title: Production recovery and guarded projection inlining (74P)
description:
# 74P — Production recovery and guarded leaf inlining

Status: complete; qualified timing deferred by user,
2026-09-12.

## Outcome

Implement the first production reconstruction operation and connect it to a
normal-path optimizer. Preserve ordinary Id semantics, the public IdApi/Method
ABI, descriptor-v2 bytes, images, owner-thread execution and native-entry barriers.
60P supplies the completed V2 control substrate. 74O supplies feasibility tests,
not production authority; this implementation must replace that distinction with
checked ownership and real driver integration.

## Bounded first consumer

Recognize a compiler-lowered, single-PC portable BlockBody whose only operations
are entry receiver/argument/capture definitions and whose terminator returns one
of those values. This includes Id methods implemented by projection blocks and
identity closures. After 64 calls, inline the return in the caller's driver:
retain the resolved active implementation, select its compiler-defined entry
slot, and commit the caller's pending Call edge without constructing a callee
Frame or invoking its StepMethod and canonical return microcode.

Target lookup remains ordinary and runs on every call. No method-name whitelist,
result cache or inference about arbitrary native code is used. Descriptor bytes
must match the admitted compiler output. Code ownership stays acquired until the
return or recovery completes. Registry eviction withdraws optimization without
invalidating an acquired activation.

The guard covers canonical Machine slot/return operations, lookup machinery and
resumable classification. Ineligible or mutated microcode recovers the original
callee at PC zero before it executes. That lets ordinary overridden operations
observe the concrete callee. The leaf has no interior callback or source-level
allocation. Preserve baseline resume-token and return-index boxing; if collection
could occur during those allocations, recover first. This avoids moving GC or
finalizer observations across an absent Frame. No source-level object allocation
is removed, and no existing identity is replaced.

This is deliberately an entry-guarded projection inline, not general inlining,
unboxing, scalar replacement or mid-body speculation. Production recovery may
admit other compiler PCs; this consumer needs only the entry recovery point.

## Recovery admission

A recovery request owns an already acquired registered callee and binds it to
one Machine, drive epoch, exact caller Frame/descriptor, pending Call edge and
result destination. It cannot import a raw descriptor pointer or executable
address from Id. The callee descriptor comes from the owned registration.

The shared floor operation validates the complete recipe before mutation:

- owner, Machine lifecycle, caller identity/epoch and exact pending Call;
- active acquired generation, descriptor identity and available pin capacity;
- callee PC, destination/source bounds, unique assignments and every live root;
- existing entry barriers and a single reconstructed child with the original
  caller and return destination retained.

Only after all checks pass may it install the child and transfer the acquired
entry to a Frame pin. Failure leaves Frames, pending edges and ownership intact.
This atomicity applies to the floor transfer; ordinary effects during recipe
decoding are retained. Transfer executes without Id sends, Birnam allocation, GC
or foreign callbacks.
Ordinary return/capture/restore/retirement subsequently own the reconstructed
Frame through their existing paths.

Expose the mechanism as the ordinary, replaceable Machine message
`recoverAt:with:` during an authorized recovery request. Its first argument is a
resume PC. Its second is an Id-described slot vector answering `size` and `at:` for each
physical destination, including explicit nil values. Decode and root these
values before the atomic transfer; revalidate authority after all Id callbacks.
The request is scoped and one-shot. Outside that scope, or with stale authority,
the operation rejects. Id policy constructs the values and chooses the resume
point; the floor checks representation and ownership, not language policy.

The optimizing consumer and the ordinary method use the same checked transfer.
The consumer can use an owned native recipe directly; the ordinary message must
also be tested with a recipe produced by Birnam code. No extra IdApi field,
external shim, image section or serialized StepAction kind is introduced.

## Implementation sequence and acceptance

1. Move the checked reconstruction core into production and add registration/pin
   admission. Keep full-state negative tests from 74O and extend ownership tests.
2. Add the scoped ordinary Id recipe operation and its rejection/GC checks.
3. Derive the projection plan from portable compiler IR, retain it through
   registration, and invoke it on hot registered Calls in the real driver.
4. Test baseline versus optimized results and identity, Machine/lookup overrides,
   target replacement, captures, GC thresholds, generation retirement, invalid
   recipes, wrong Machine/epoch and one-shot use. Exercise compiler-generated
   artifacts and ordinary Id recipe construction, including source-independent
   compilation. Retain V2 capture/restore and native participation regressions.
5. Measure a warmed projection-heavy fixture with independent baseline/control
   and optimized runs. Separate warmup, steady execution, allocations and actual
   inline/recovery counts. Host-gated timing must be accepted before claiming a
   speed benefit; correctness and implementation completion are separate facts.
6. Run debug/release tests, frozen-authority checks and the full production gate;
   record commands, source hashes, counts and measured results. Update tracker,
   changelog and current design navigation. No commit/push is implied by this task.

Do not expand to general inlining until this slice has both a correct recovery
contract and measurements identifying its actual benefit or bottleneck.

## Implementation decisions

The production core lives in `execution/recovery.rs`; the old 74O module retains
only test snapshots. Registration acquisitions are checked before transfer and
become Frame pins only after complete admission. The scoped Machine operation
roots decoded values in reverse-release order and revalidates the caller after
Id sends. The first consumer uses an owned dense native recipe through the same
engine; an independently compiled captured Id block supplies an ordinary recipe
in the integration test.

The inline does not cache target lookup. It avoids a callee Frame, StepMethod
entry and canonical return dispatch. It preserves PC/slot boxing and the
reflective scratch ReturnAction. A persistent microcode guard miss reconstructs
once, then uses baseline entry until dictionary mutation permits another attempt.
A collection-boundary miss is retried after collection rather than permanently
withdrawing the optimization.

The executable test fixture compiles both caller and callee from portable
CodePrograms and registers them through production staging. It covers argument
and capture identity, exact allocation-byte equality, overridden return/lookup,
private Machines, GC observing the reconstructed callee, current target changes,
non-entry recovery, an Id-authored captured recipe, one-shot scope, malformed
recipes, stale authority, capture/restore and generation retirement. A separate
installed-prefix fixture materializes actual Birnam source-independent code,
warms it, evicts the compilation cache and collects before checking identity again.

Timing uses one release test binary with independently selected baseline/inline
records, identical compiler artifacts and an unoptimized control body. It records
warmup and steady execution separately and checks actual hit/recovery counters.
`python3 scripts/production-recovery.py --measure --verify` runs all checks; the
repository host gate requires AC power and acceptable competing load. Battery
measurements do not qualify a speed claim.

## Lifetime regression exposed by integration

The installed-prefix lifecycle gate initially retained one extra native Unit.
Root tracing identified a pending retirement generation ID on the conservative
native stack: JIT IDs were the exact Unit payload address. Adding the recovery
selector changed allocation layout enough to expose this existing self-rooting
hazard, even with the optimizer disabled. JIT generation keys now tag the aligned
Unit address with bit zero set, so the scalar key cannot match an Oop payload
address. Generated carriers, staging, cache eviction and rebuilt images use the
same key. Explicit Unit references and generation leases remain the ownership
authority; mapped generation IDs and serialized artifact formats are unchanged.
The unchanged portable lifecycle smoke now passes with production recovery enabled.

## Verification record

`python3 scripts/production-recovery.py --verify` completed with exit zero.
[The receipt](../measurements/74p-production-recovery.json) records source hashes,
frozen ABI/descriptor/image authorities and complete command output:

- All three production integration tests pass in debug and release, with ten
  matching result rows in each profile.
- The complete workspace passes: 458 tests, zero failures, 12 intentionally
  ignored experiments. Native-prefix, image/lifecycle, V2 control, two independent
  cold archives and relocated-runtime gates also pass.
- Argument and capture fixtures each record 16 warmed inline hits, with identical
  baseline/optimized allocation totals of 11,648 bytes. These are work/identity
  checks, not a wall-clock speed claim.
- New Rust files pass formatting checks; the Python runner and shell hook pass
  syntax checks; `git diff --check` is clean.

[The earlier timing attempt](../measurements/74p-timing-blocked-battery.json)
was rejected by the host gate before any timing samples: the machine was on
battery. That receipt describes an earlier source snapshot, before the lifetime
fix; it is retained only as evidence of the timing blocker. The temporarily
paused `rk` process was resumed. No qualified speedup is claimed.

Implementation and correctness work are complete. The user explicitly requested
completion without qualified timings; `birnam-06p` is closed on that basis. The
seven paired projection/fallback/control measurements remain a future performance
follow-up, with no speedup claim. Run
`python3 scripts/production-recovery.py --measure --verify` on a qualified host
before broadening the optimizer. Changes are not committed or pushed by this task.

title: Compiler-generated small-callee recovery plans (74R)
description:
# 74R — Compiler-generated small-callee recovery plans

Status: implemented and correctness-verified, 2026-09-12. Qualified performance
acceptance remains a follow-up because competing host load failed admission.

## Authorized batch

Implement Stage 1 of [74Q](74q-optimization-roadmap.md) after checkpoint
`d15a40ce`: extend 74P to bounded single-PC BlockBodies composed of entry
receiver/argument/capture values and local `Bind` aliases ending in Return.
No nested inlining, source allocation elimination, target cache, changed ABI,
canonical descriptor encoding or image format is included.

## Compiler and runtime contract

The compiler derives an immutable process-local plan from logical definitions
and their colored physical slots. It traces each alias to its original entry
value, records the physical return slot separately, and describes PC-zero
recovery with explicit entry-slot or nil sources for every physical destination.
Recovery restores baseline entry state, not a partially evaluated alias body.
The plan also records the exact baseline boxing order: each Bind's destination
index before its source index, then the return index. Runtime PC-token boxing
remains unchanged. At most 32 operations and 64 physical slots are admitted; typed refusal
reasons distinguish region shape, limits, observing operations and invalid layouts.

The runtime validates the canonical descriptor against the admitted compilation
and retains the plan with its weakly indexed registration. A successful hot call
uses the returned entry value without constructing a callee Frame. It preserves
all baseline index boxes, allocation order and reflective ReturnAction contents.
It checks the whole boxing budget before execution; a possible collection or an
observing/overridden Machine operation recovers first through production admission.
Existing targets remain resolved afresh and code acquisitions remain owned until
return or transfer. No guard miss may execute aliases twice or expose a missing
Frame. Unsupported operations and non-entry continuation shapes decline.

The compiler plan is ordinary data (slot sources, boxed indices and return
locations), not privileged language policy. The existing Id-described dense
recipe operation remains the floor interface; the new compiler producer feeds
the same one-shot checked recovery transfer.

## Acceptance and measurement

- Compare argument/capture aliases, chains and distinct colored slots against canonical
  compiled baseline code. Preserve exact Oop identity and boxing values/order.
- Override Machine reads, writes, return and lookup; verify callee observations,
  ordered effects and current-target replacement. Exercise GC before any alias
  boxing can collect, plus refusal for calls, literals and other observing work.
- Keep malformed/stale recovery, ownership, capture/restore and generation
  retirement regressions from 74P. Run debug/release and full production gates.
- Measure baseline, 74P-only admission and the new pass separately, with
  projection, alias, ineligible and persistent-guard-miss controls. Report cold
  preparation/warmup, steady time, allocations and actual hits/recoveries.
- Use qualified host gates when available. The user permits unqualified battery
  measurements; label those receipts explicitly and retain the measured spread.
  Pause the previously authorized `rk` process only during timing and resume it
  with guaranteed cleanup. No speedup is assumed before measurement.

## Implemented mechanism

The pure compiler pass lives in
[`small_callee.rs`](../../rust/birnam-codegen/src/small_callee.rs), and production
selection consumes it in
[`native_tier.rs`](../../rust/birnam-id/src/runtime/native_tier.rs). Plans contain
no Oops or executable addresses and do not introduce a new recipe category at the
Id boundary: their entry-slot/nil sources populate the existing dense slot recipe.
The existing compiled Id recipe, stale-admission, capture/restore and retirement
regressions remain passing.

For a three-alias argument body, the entry source is slot 1 and the final return
location is slot 4. The plan retains that distinction. Entry recovery initializes
slots 0 and 1 from their original Oops and explicitly sets alias slots 2–4 to nil;
baseline execution then performs the bindings. Successful inlining returns the
original slot-1 Oop and publishes a ReturnAction naming slot 4. The canonical
boxing sequence is `[2, 1, 3, 2, 4, 3, 4]`, plus the existing driver PC token.

The current one-PC coloring keeps the step-safepoint union live, so these alias
slots are distinct. This batch does not claim reconstruction under a future,
more aggressive slot-reuse algorithm. Likewise, larger/multi-PC bodies, sends,
literals, global reads and closure construction remain outside this pass.

A GC-budget regression leaves enough allocation room for the old projection's
two boxes but not the alias sequence. The candidate must reconstruct before the
sequence begins; actual collection then observes the callee at depth two. Tests
also compare the complete canonical index-box sequence, change results through
custom reads, observe writes/return, replace lookup and the current target, and
prove an observing source send executes exactly once.

## Correctness evidence

`python3 scripts/small-callee.py --verify` completed with exit zero.
[The receipt](../measurements/74r-correctness.json) contains source hashes,
frozen-authority checks and all command output:

- Two compiler tests and six production runtime tests pass in debug and release;
  the 17 runtime result rows agree across profiles.
- All 463 workspace tests pass, with zero failures and 13 intentionally ignored
  experiments. No compiler warnings were emitted by these runs.
- Native-prefix, named/block generation lifetime, image-v8, V2 control, two cold
  source archives and relocated-runtime gates pass.
- The installed source-independent
  [fixture](../../scripts/fixtures/small-callee-recovery.birnam) checks alias and
  captured Cell identity, exactly-once effects, cache eviction and GC.
- Sixteen three-alias calls allocate the same 13,184 Id-heap bytes in baseline and
  optimized modes. All 256 observed body/caller index boxes agree in order/value;
  optimized mode records 16 hits. Two calls under read/write overrides produce
  exactly 12 callee read/write effects and reconstruct once before cached fallback.

The canonical public ABI, descriptors, baseline C emitter and image authorities
match checkpoint `d15a40ce`. The small-callee data is private, regenerated metadata.
The 74P runner now selects its original three tests explicitly, and its historical
control retains 74P eligibility even though the alias body is now optimizable.

## Measurements and limits

AC power became available, but both qualified attempts failed the host gate:
[the first](../measurements/74r-host-rejected-load.json) had 22.61% median idle CPU
with another compiler above the per-process limit;
[the second](../measurements/74r-host-rejected-load-repeat.json) had 4.45% median
idle CPU and other busy processes. No host threshold was weakened. The authorized
`rk` pause was confined to timing attempts and the process was resumed afterward.

[Seven exploratory pairs](../measurements/74r-unqualified-timing.json) completed
with 10,000 calls per sample. All 133 samples passed their identity, allocation,

# 74S — Dispatch specialization, redundant work and native optimization

Status: implementation in progress. Authorized goal: implement the next three
optimization families after the first inlining batch and measure each separately.
The starting checkpoint is `d06f7558` (74R). This document records the concrete
contracts before implementation; passing experiments do not imply whole-program
performance acceptance.

## Sequence and acceptance

1. Specialized dispatch: retain the resolved canonical method for a repeated
   receiver-vtable/selector pair, avoiding repeated dictionary/delegation walks.
   A bounded runtime cache admits one receiver shape per selector bucket. This
   is shared dispatch specialization, not yet per-source-call-site profiling.
   Guard the current canonical lookup operation, global dictionary/delegation
   mutation epoch, receiver vtable and selector. Do not cache unknown lookup,
   exhausted epochs or unbound results. Preserve normal target classification,
   acquisitions and invocation. Discard address-only entries before GC/retirement
   tracing and prohibit refill during collection, so cache metadata neither roots
   objects nor keeps code alive. Mutation and collector hooks remain ordinary
   observation boundaries. Test inherited lookup, replacement/removal, parent
   changes, custom and resumable lookup, native reentry, GC and generation lifetime.
2. Redundant reads/computations: derive bounded observation-free regions from
   canonical lowering. Reuse repeated physical Frame reads only while writes,
   allocation/GC, lookup mutation, reentry and Machine overrides cannot invalidate
   the value. Retain every baseline box and every live recovery-visible value.
   Profile the proposed region before choosing the concrete producer/consumer;
   isolated 74H read reuse did not demonstrate a win.
3. Conventional native optimization: eliminate redundant native copies and dead
   implementation temporaries within the derived representation, preserving all
   semantic operations, allocation order and baseline recovery state. Choose the
   concrete pass from the preceding region profile. No source allocation or
   numeric identity change is part of this family.

Each family requires independent on/off timings against the preceding family,
combined results, controls and mutation/churn coverage. Save source/binary hashes,
actual hits/misses/recoveries, preparation, metadata size and allocation totals.

`rk` process and always resume it. Keep 74R fallback/control and preparation costs
visible (`birnam-bew`). Preserve public ABI, descriptors, image format, full Id
malleability, stackless control and code lifetime. Later family contracts will be
made concrete before their code changes, with evidence recorded here.

title: Implement numeric, loop, aggregate and closure optimization families
description:
# 74T — Numeric, loop, aggregate and closure optimization

Status: implementation in progress. This document tracks the user's request to
implement all four remaining families in [74Q](74q-optimization-roadmap.md).
Recovery infrastructure alone does not complete a family. The outstanding 74S
application timing gate remains separate.

## Contract

Preserve ordinary Id meaning, mutable method lookup, object identity, shared
Cells, observable Frames, stackless control and active native-code ownership.
No selector or prototype name grants intrinsic authority. The public IdApi,
Method ABI, canonical descriptors and image formats remain unchanged.

Compiler eligibility and recovery descriptions must be producible using
ordinary Id objects. Runtime admission validates storage, roots, authority and
lifetime; it does not turn a producer's semantic assertion into trusted proof.
An optimizer must independently establish that the operation being replaced is
the operation for which it has a guarded summary.

The existing code establishes two constraints that govern implementation:

- `birnam-prelude::numeric_binary` uses signed 128-bit intermediates for integer
  addition, subtraction and multiplication, then checks the signed 64-bit range.
  Division also checks zero and range; mixed arithmetic converts to floating
  point. Error operands and operator redefinition remain ordinary behavior.
- The floor exposes live allocation counts and triggers automatic collection
  using allocated bytes. Non-escape alone cannot authorize allocation removal.
  Removing an allocation must preserve observations at subsequent boundaries,
  including GC timing and finalizers; suppressing collection is not a proof.

## Implementation sequence and completion evidence

| Work | Required production behavior | Evidence required before completion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared recovery | Validated acyclic identity graphs, existing Oop inputs, exact numeric bits, one materialization per virtual identity; roots survive collecting materialization and publication stays atomic | Invalid and stale recipes; repeated aliases versus equal distinct objects; GC between construction steps; Id-authored recipes; capture/restore and native retirement |
| Unboxed arithmetic | Derive numeric chains from current admitted implementations; carry raw intermediate values with exact overflow/error rules and materialize at observation boundaries | Integer extrema, zero division, mixed numeric/error operands, changed operators and lookup, forced exits at every supported point; separate arithmetic and allocation accounting |
| Loop optimization | Recognize actual Id control behavior; remove invariant work within bounded execution intervals, preserving ordinary mutation and stackless transition boundaries | Representative loop, effects once and in order, invariant invalidation, suspension/capture responsiveness, guard overhead and profitable execution |
| Temporary-object elimination | Derive escape, identity and allocation-observation proofs for acyclic aggregates; scalar-replace private fields and materialize before exposure | Actual allocation savings, shared graph identity, reflective/native escape, collection during materialization, finalizer/collection threshold counterexamples |
| Closure/capture elimination | Derive a directly invoked private closure and substitute its environment into the admitted body; retain shared mutable Cells | Actual closure allocation savings, multiple uses and escaping fallbacks, shared Cell updates, method replacement, native observation and continuation capture |

These are implementation obligations, not a claim that every source program is
optimizable. Unsupported or unstable cases execute canonical code. Broader shapes
must use the same analysis and recovery contracts; passing a synthetic kernel
does not stand in for an installed compiler consumer.

## Recovery graph

The compiler representation separates input identities from newly constructed
identities. A value reference selects an existing input or an earlier graph node.
Every node denotes one fresh identity even when two nodes have equal numeric
values. Multiple references to one node must resolve to the same Oop. Nodes are
ordered before their users, so cycles and forward references are rejected before
Birnam allocation. Graphs explicitly describe every destination Frame slot.

Initial node shapes are exact signed integers, exact floating-point bits and
all-Oop aggregates with an existing vtable input. Existing objects, including
captured Cells, are retained as inputs. Raw storage, finalizers and trace hooks
require additional contracts and are not inferred from a producer's description.
Closure-specific construction must also retain its registered implementation and
capture layout; an arbitrary aggregate is not automatically a valid closure.

Structural validation is pure compiler code with fixed node, input, slot and
field limits. Runtime validation checks the actual heap and layout before
materialization. All inputs and constructed nodes stay precisely rooted until
the complete graph has been installed or rejected. Allocating construction and
callback-free Frame publication are separate phases. Recovery authority is
revalidated after any phase that can run foreign code.

## Verification and measurements

For each family retain a canonical source fixture, pass-off and pass-on modes,
forced recovery points and ineligible/mutation controls. Run debug and release
differential checks over values, identities, errors, ordered effects and resource
lifetime. Complete the source-build, installed-prefix, image, cold archive and
relocation gates before calling the production change verified.

Record hits, misses, recovery counts, allocations, retained memory, code/metadata
size and preparation cost, plus paired cold/warm/steady timings. Host qualification
uses the existing thresholds. A noisy host can delay qualified timing but does
not justify dropping implementation or correctness obligations.

## Progress

- Implementation contracts checked against current lowering, numeric primitives,
  allocation accounting and production recovery.
- Identity graph validation and materialization are the first implementation
  dependency. No remaining optimization family is complete yet.
